items.title: Josh Shapiro Is Looking Past His Own Reelection
items.description: C harles Benjamin voted for the first time in 2024, casting a ballot for President Trump. Since then, he’s watched his McDonald’s order—two McDoubles and large fries—go up seven bucks. His Red Bulls cost more too. One of his fraternity brothers at East Stroudsburg University, who’s in the military, just shipped off to the Middle East to support a war that Benjamin believed Trump had promised not to start. “I don’t appreciate that he lied,” Benjamin, a 21-year-old junior sporting a leopard-print sweatshirt and holding a lacrosse stick, told me. I met Benjamin as he was waiting to see Josh Shapiro at a campus rally. Benjamin was curious about the Pennsylvania governor, but unsure whether to vote for him. The event got off to a lackluster start. A few dozen people stood around a small stage set out on the quad as students walked to class behind them, ignoring the speeches from local Democratic officials. Then Shapiro came out. He talked about high prices and the Iran war and corruption among elected officials. “I understand that there are some of you who showed up today with a little bit of healthy cynicism, a little bit of healthy skepticism, wondering, Is anything ever really going to change? ” Shapiro said. Yes, he told the crowd—but only if you care, and only if you vote. Benjamin and his friend Nick Vyprynyuk, a volunteer firefighter with disheveled strawberry-blonde hair who had also cast his ballot for Trump in 2024, listened carefully. By the end, Shapiro had won their votes. He was “electrifying,” Vyprynyuk, a senior, told me. “I like how enthusiastic he was.” Michelle Gustafson for The Atlantic Supporters cheer as Governor Josh Shapiro speaks at the Flip PA-01 Rally with Bob Harvie in Doylestown, Pennsylvania. Shapiro’s exuberance on the stump, in speeches that channel the optimistic pragmatism of former President Obama (not to mention his speaking cadence ), could help explain the Democratic governor’s popularity in Pennsylvania, a state that voted for Trump in 2016 and 2024. Shapiro has been able to feed deep-blue Democrats’ loathing of Trump while assembling a coalition that is large enough to include people who voted for the president. It’s an effective strategy: Polls regularly show him leading Republican Stacy Garrity, the MAGA-aligned state treasurer, by more than 20 points. (Garrity is pledging to “fix the problems Josh Shapiro has created,” including Pennsylvania’s relatively high tax burden and rising food prices.) Shapiro’s lead is larger than his margin of victory in 2022 against state Senator Doug Mastriano, who had a history of espousing far right-conspiracy theories and associating with Islamophobes and anti-Semites. Shapiro spent last week touring the state, with a focus on trying to win over rural voters—though actual Republicans tended to be elusive at his rallies. In Pike County, the ruby-red gateway to the Poconos, Trump won by 24 points two years ago. Few, if any, of the president’s supporters showed up to see the governor. In Milford, a tiny town in the state’s northeast corner, it was die-hard Democrats only—including the organizer of the town’s self-proclaimed “Resistance Committee,” a group that spends Wednesday afternoons in the center of town protesting Trump, and a guy in a Grateful Dead–themed Make America Grateful Again sweatshirt. Shapiro told people to take two signs on their way out—one to stick in their front yard that day, and another to replace it a day or two later, after their neighbors steal the first. “Smile when you put it back out there,” Shapiro said. “That sends a message to your neighbors: You’re not going to be messed with.” Even when Trump acolytes don’t show up, Shapiro is trying to send a message to rural voters: I’m looking out for you. Inside an old hunting and fishing lodge in Pennsylvania coal country, Shapiro bragged about ending the state’s century-old ban on hunting on Sundays. When he appeared at a small gym at a community college near Wilkes-Barre, Shapiro boasted of writing an executive order that heavily regulates the construction of AI data centers after hearing from concerned residents of a nearby community. [ From the November 2026 issue: The great data-center rebellion ] Shapiro’s campaign slogan is GSD, for “get shit done,” and that message plays to a broad swath of the state, said Danny Ceisler, the Democratic sheriff of Bucks County. He told me that Shapiro is “the antidote to what everybody hates about politics.” Ceisler unseated a Republican incumbent in the purple suburban county last year after criticizing his decision to partner with ICE. Ceisler said Shapiro’s ability to make things happen—including hiring more cops statewide—has earned him the respect and support of many law-enforcement officers. Michelle Gustafson for The Atlantic Shapiro greets attendees of the Montgomery County Grassroots Rally in Gilbertsville, Pennsylvania. Shapiro told me that achieving success as a Democrat in a purple state really is as straightforward as getting shit done. “Show up, especially in communities that didn’t vote for you. Treat people with respect. Listen to them and maybe why they made a different choice, and then do. Go back to the office and deliver for them,” he said outside the hunting lodge, which was in Schuylkill County and surrounded by crisp red-and-yellow maple leaves. It’s not a very satisfying answer—and it sounds a lot like what all politicians say is a winning formula. But Shapiro is betting that he can make that message resonate outside of his own race—and far beyond Pennsylvania. Four more years in Harrisburg to keep GSD-ing looks like a given, so he’s using his campaign to try to flip four swing congressional districts in Pennsylvania. Shapiro has tied his political future to the success of Scranton Mayor Paige Cognetti, Janelle Stelson in south-central Pennsylvania, Bob Harvie in Bucks County, and Bob Brooks in the Lehigh Valley. They’re all Democrats trying to defeat incumbent Republican members of Congress. The effort is personal for Shapiro, who took credit for recruiting the Democrats to run. If he can help pull them over the line, he’ll have significant bragging rights for 2026—and one more achievement to tout if, as expected, he runs for president in 2028. S hapiro’s all-in support for the four is as telling as his calculations about which Democratic candidates not to fully back. At the hunting lodge in Schuylkill County, he spoke at the same event as Rachel Wallace, a Democrat running against Republican Dan Meuser. (Meuser accused Shapiro of lying about cuts to food assistance and health insurance in his speech at the lodge, claiming his remarks show a “lack of moral character.”) But Meuser’s seat is considered safe—he won by more than 40 points two years ago—and Shapiro knows it. He said he wants to see Wallace win but did not give her the kind of full-throttle endorsement he gave the other four. He recently created a federal political-action committee so he could funnel donations to the candidates he’s supporting, and Wallace is not among them. The vibe is different for the candidates he wants to help win; Shapiro often notes that Democrats need just four seats to flip control in the House. Standing beside Cognetti last week in Milford, he told the crowd, “You have the ability, by electing her, to literally put the Democrats in charge of the Congress and deliver a check against this president.” The next night, he told 200 people in a Teamsters parking lot that electing Stelson—a former Lancaster news anchor who narrowly lost a congressional race against the same competitor, the incumbent Scott Perry, two years ago—“quite literally will tilt the balance of power in Washington.” Michelle Gustafson for The Atlantic Campaign signs outside the Bucks County Democratic Committee office in Doylestown, Pennsylvania As I followed Shapiro’s bus tour through the Poconos and the Blue Mountains, I asked Cognetti, Stelson, and Wallace about how Shapiro—an anti-Trump Democrat from the liberal Philadelphia suburbs who spends a good portion of every speech slamming the president’s “chaos, cruelty, and corruption”—has won the backing of so many Republicans. (A New York Times /Siena poll in September found Shapiro winning support from a fifth of self-identified Republican voters.) Cognetti told me it’s because Shapiro is not a partisan in the way he governs; he appointed Republicans to his administration and has worked with the Republican-controlled state Senate. She’s been trying to convince voters that she does the same. “He doesn’t run the government of Pennsylvania in a hyper-partisan way,” she told me in a classroom at East Stroudsburg. “Similarly, I don’t run the city of Scranton in a partisan way.” Wallace, a longtime Democratic staffer who returned to Schuylkill County a few years ago when her mom was diagnosed with Parkinson’s disease, told me the lesson she takes from Shapiro is to show up. Stelson, who calls Shapiro “the other J.S.,” said his success stems from his work ethic. “He works for all of us, and that’s the kind of representative I’d like to be as well,” Stelson said before taking the stage outside the local Teamsters headquarters near Harrisburg. For Shapiro, his investment in the House races is a clever way to make an impact on national politics without the speculation that comes from visiting early presidential-primary states such as New Hampshire or South Carolina. But his casual manner in front of a crowd, even in impromptu speeches, masks his strict message discipline. Those close to him know not to feed the 2028 rumors, and to stick to the Shapiro line: Keep it local. [ Read: The operator ] Stelson was the only one of the congressional candidates willing to even acknowledge that Shapiro’s dreams might be bigger than Pennsylvania, when praising his ability to quickly reopen I-95 after an overpass collapsed in Philadelphia in 2023. “He’ll be talking about that, you know, should he ever decide to run for higher office or anything,” she told me, before stopping herself. “ Should he ever,” Stelson said with a wink. An hour later, Shapiro walked onstage at the Teamsters rally. He closed his speech by reminding attendees that Philadelphia hosted the Constitutional Convention, and the city was where the Founders signed the Declaration of Independence. He talked about the promise of democracy and the work that individual Americans must do to keep it alive. It’s a story with special resonance in Pennsylvania—and one that would play pretty well in South Carolina too.

items.title: Burkina Faso : 93 militaires et agents des Eaux et Forêts retraités outillés pour leur reconversion dans l’agropastoral
items.description: Le ministère de la Guerre et de la Défense patriotique a procédé, ce 3 novembre 2026 au camp Guillaume Ouédraogo à Ouagadougou, à l’ouverture officielle de la 18e session de formation en Agriculture et en élevage au profit des militaires en phase de reconversion. Ces sessions de formation s'inscrivent dans le cadre du programme de reconversion des militaires mis en œuvre depuis 2013 pour accompagner les militaires retraités dans une autre carrière. L'édition 2026 des sessions de formation en agriculture et en élevage au profit des militaires en phase de reconversion a enregistré 93 projets, dont ceux de 83 personnels militaires et de 10 personnels des Eaux et Forêts. Pendant trois semaines, les futurs retraités, répartis entre Ouagadougou et Bobo-Dioulasso, seront outillés en techniques et pratiques agricoles afin d’être aptes à réussir leur reconversion. Pour ce faire, le Cabinet CID Ingénierie, chargé de la formation, a élaboré des modules spécifiques. Il s'agira entre autres, des techniques de production agricole adaptées aux conditions agroécologiques du Burkina, de la préparation des sols, de la gestion de leur fertilité et de l'utilisation raisonnée des engrais. Les participants vont aborder également les principes fondamentaux de l'élevage, de l'alimentation animale, de l'hygiène, de la prévention des maladies et la gestion économique d'une exploitation agricole et d'une unité d'élevage. Le présidium de la cérémonie©️Faso7 « Aujourd'hui, votre champ de bataille change. Il se déplace des lignes de défense vers les champs de culture et les exploitations agro-pastorales. Cette formation en agriculture et en élevage que nous lançons aujourd'hui est conçue pour être le catalyseur de votre reconversion. Elle vise à vous donner les clés de votre autonomie financière et de votre épanouissement socioprofessionnel », a expliqué l’Intendant Colonel-major Yamba Léonard Ouoba, Secrétaire Général du ministère de la Guerre et de la Défense Patriotique. Il a fait comprendre aux retraités qu'après le service militaire, ils sont appelés à servir la nation sous d'autres formes. Les différentes qualités et aptitudes qu'ils ont acquises durant leur vie professionnelle doivent être mises à profit pour faire d'eux des producteurs exemplaires. « Investir dans la reconversion de nos forces de défense est un impératif moral et économique. En devenant des acteurs clés du secteur agropastoral, ces futurs retraités et retraités participeront activement à la lutte pour l'autosuffisance alimentaire. Ils deviendront des créateurs d’emplois et des modèles de réussite pour la jeunesse », a-t-il ajouté. Le directeur de cabinet du ministère chargé de l’Agriculture, Alassane Guiré, parrain de cette cohorte, a rappelé la convention-cadre existant entre son département et celui de la Défense patriotique. Celle-ci a pour objectif d'accompagner au moins 1 000 militaires en cinq ans. Évoquant la place centrale de l'agriculture au sein des pays sahéliens, il a souligné que plus de sept actifs sur dix y travaillent, principalement au sein d'exploitations familiales. Au cours de ces sessions, le ministère chargé de l’Agriculture se chargera de former les retraités aux techniques de production et de faciliter leur installation à l'issue de la formation. Le département leur apportera également un appui pour leur organisation en coopératives ainsi que pour l'accès au financement, au foncier et à l'eau. « Chaque champ bien conduit, chaque troupeau bien tenu est une part de notre souveraineté. Votre choix n'a donc rien d'un repli. Il rejoint celui de la plupart des militaires admis à la retraite qui se réorientent vers ce secteur pour produire, transformer et commercialiser. Personne ici ne vous promet une gloire facile. Mais sachez que vous avez ce que beaucoup de débutants n'ont pas : la discipline, l'endurance et le sens de la nation », a-t-il expliqué. Pour joindre l’acte à la parole, le parrain a offert à ses filleuls 12 tonnes d’intrants agricoles, composées de 3 tonnes d’engrais NPK, de 2 tonnes d’engrais urée, de 2 tonnes de tourteau de soja, de 2 tonnes de tourteau de coton, de 3 tonnes d’aliments pour poissons, ainsi que divers matériels techniques. Rappelons que le programme de reconversion des militaires a, depuis sa mise en œuvre, contribué à insérer 974 militaires en entreprise et à former 1 529 autres en agriculture, en élevage, en élaboration de business plans et en gestion d’entreprise. Par ailleurs, il a octroyé un prêt de 586 191 000 F CFA à 236 militaires pour le financement de leurs projets professionnels. Cheick Habib Désiré BAYILI Faso7 L’article Burkina Faso : 93 militaires et agents des Eaux et Forêts retraités outillés pour leur reconversion dans l’agropastoral est apparu en premier sur Faso7 .

items.title: TikTok Dance: Feminist group slams Hisbah over arrest Of 3 women in Kano
items.description: By John Alechenu ABUJA-The Feminist Digital Watch (FemDigital Watch) has condemned the arrest and arraignment of popular TikTok creator Amani Ishaq and two others by the Kano State Hisbah Board over dance videos posted on social media. The collective, convened by the Redefining Alternative Civic Engagement for Africa (RACE Centre), said Hauwa Khamis and Sa’adatu Muhammad were arrested alongside Ishaq for allegedly contravening public morality and religious guidelines. They were arraigned before Magistrate Court No. 5, Court Road, Kano. This was contained in a statement signed by Evelyn Ugbe on behalf of the collective, in Abuja, on Tuesday. FemDigital Watch said while charges, bail conditions and detention status were still being verified, the incident marks a “troubling escalation in the systemic surveillance and criminalization of women’s creative self-expression in digital spaces.” According to the group, the targeting of the three women is not isolated enforcement of local ordinances but reflects an entrenched pattern of technology-facilitated, gender-based suppression. “Across Nigeria’s digital ecosystem, women creators consistently face disproportionate scrutiny, online mobbing, and state-backed censorship for routine digital expression that is widely normalized for men,” the statement said. The group said weaponization of morality laws to police women’s online participation shrinks civic and creative space for female creators who rely on platforms like TikTok for livelihood, encourages coordinated online abuse, and undermines constitutional rights. It said the action conflicts with Section 39 of the 1999 Constitution (as amended) which guarantees freedom of expression and Nigeria’s obligations under the Maputo Protocol. FemDigital Watch demanded immediate, unhindered access to legal representation and equitable bail terms for the three women and respect for their fundamental human rights without moral prejudice. It also called on the Kano State Hisbah Board and regulatory authorities to cease arbitrary surveillance, arrest and detention of female content creators exercising their right to peaceful freedom of expression and bodily autonomy online. The collective said it is documenting state-enforced and tech-facilitated abuses against women and girls and mobilizing legal-defense partners and civil society networks to track proceedings in Kano. items.title: Ghanaian consumer packaged goods increased by 8.9% in half-year 2026 – Maverick Research
items.description: Recent data from Maverick Research, which measures Consumer Packaged Goods (CPG) performance across West African markets, shows that Ghanaian CPG volumes increased by 8.9% in the first half of 2026, alongside value growth of 15.6%. This shows West Africa’s emerging CPG growth opportunity, particularly in Ghana and Nigeria. For several years, impressive-looking value growth across many emerging markets has often been heavily influenced by inflation. Maverick Research said consumers in Ghana are now not simply paying more, adding, “They are buying more”. According to the market research firm, the composition of that growth is equally revealing. Food increased its share of CPG volume from 32.2% to 34.2%, with edible oil, tomato paste, milk, noodles and food seasonings among the categories driving the recovery. Improving purchasing power, easing inflation and a stronger cedi have helped consumers rebuild their baskets. Yet the recovery is not simply a Ghana story. Maverick’s data also showed Côte d’Ivoire recording approximately 3% volume growth in the first half of 2026 and Cameroon 2.7%. Maverick Research continued that West Africa is not one consumer market, saying different countries — and increasingly different regions and cities within those countries — are moving at different speeds and responding to different economic forces. Opportunity is Significant Itstated that the opportunity is significant, but winning requires a different playbook. Perhaps, it argued that the most interesting evidence comes from companies already succeeding in the region. It cited Nestlé as a good example. Rather than treating West Africa simply as an export market, Maverick Research said the company has built substantial local capabilities and adapted global brands to local consumers. “MAGGI has become deeply embedded in West African cooking, while MILO illustrates how a global brand can be adapted to local tastes and supply chains. Nestlé has used locally sourced ingredients in market-specific formulations and built manufacturing capabilities across the region”. It added that availability is strongly associated with market share. “In other words, in Ghana, being available isn’t simply an execution metric. It is strongly associated with winning”. “The experience of individual brands reinforces the point. 80% of Ghana’s five biggest share gainers over the past two years — Viju, Verna, Malta Guinness, Geisha and Bigoo — expanded their distribution. While pricing also mattered for some brands, wider availability was the most consistent factor separating the winners”, it alluded. Maverick Research also identified brands such as Milo, Cerelac and Lipton whose rate of sale significantly exceeds what their distribution alone might predict — suggesting that availability and genuine consumer pull need to work together.

items.title: 'We made a deal months ago': Trump says US will stop $4 billion funding to Israel at end of 2026
items.description: US President Donald Trump on Tuesday said he made a deal with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu that Washington would stop $4 billion in funding to Israel after the end of this year. Speaking to Fox News ’ ‘Fox and Friends’, Trump said Israel no longer needed the funding and that some Democrats and left-wing politicians were using the US financial support to Israel as a talking point to criticise Republicans. “Now, as far as paying Israel, Bibi Netanyahu and I have made a deal that we give Israel $4bn a year, and we made a deal months ago that we’re stopping,” Trump told the broadcaster. “We’ve already agreed that by the end of this year we won’t be paying Israel. Now we’ll help Israel if they need it.” There was no immediate comment from Netanyahu’s office on Trump’s remarks. It was not immediately clear which exact funding Trump meant. A memorandum of understanding that provides $3.8bn in annual US military aid to Israel is approaching its expiration date in 2028, and conversations have been under way on how Washington’s assistance to Israel would evolve beyond that date. “They can buy whatever they want. They can buy whatever they want. So can Europe. We make the greatest weapons in the world,” Trump added. Netanyahu said in a May interview with CBS that he hoped to wean Israel off US military support within a decade. In a June letter to a US congressman, he wrote that the time had come for Israel “to move from aid recipient to partner”. US public support for Israel has fallen since the Gaza war began in 2023, particularly among Democrats. A June Quinnipiac University poll found 48 per cent of voters and 66pc of Democrats believe the United States is too supportive of Israel, up from 16pc and 20pc when the question was first asked in 2017. Support for Israel among Democratic voters has plummeted, candidates critical of Israel are winning Democratic primaries, and even moderate lawmakers are increasingly willing to challenge decades of US support for Israel. “The left uses the $4bn payment that everybody knows about — well, it’s no secret — as a signal of unfairness, and we can’t allow that to happen,” Trump said. “We were giving them $4bn, we are, but it gets cut off at the end of the year. Why? Because they don’t need it.”

items.title: Americans vote in midterms set to upend Trump presidency
items.description: Americans voted on Tuesday in pivotal midterm elections, with Democrats hoping to seize control of Congress and impose the first significant checks on Donald Trump’s chaotic second term in the White House. Multiple polls predict Democrats will take control of the House of Representatives and have a shot at seizing the Senate on the back of voter resentment at a deeply unpopular president, soaring energy costs and the dragging conflict with Iran. Republicans losing the House would give Democrats the power to stall Trump’s legislative agenda and launch sweeping investigations of his administration. A Senate defeat would also threaten his ability to appoint Supreme Court justices and senior officials. Voters cast their ballots inside a polling location in the social hall at St Patrick’s Church on November 3, 2026 in Youngstown, Ohio. — AFP The election amounts to a nationwide judgment on Trump, with the mood turning sharply against Republicans amid anger over soaring living costs and the war on Iran. All 435 House seats and 35 of the 100 Senate seats are at stake, along with governorships in 36 states. Democrats need only three House gains and a net four seats in the Senate to wrest both chambers from Republican hands. Trump returned to office last year promising to bring down prices, but inflation, tariffs and fuel costs inflated by the Middle East conflict have squeezed Americans. A person holds a sticker, during the US midterm elections, in Durham, North Carolina, US, November 3. — Reuters The 80-year-old’s approval rating has hovered near the low 30s. In the suburbs of Atlanta, Georgia, retired teacher Jane Callum, 77, was among Democrats canvassing for Senator Jon Ossoff, who framed the race as a watershed moment for the country’s future. “I really feel an obligation to do everything that I possibly can to change the direction that our country is going in now, and put it more on the path to democracy and away from autocracy,” she told AFP . Economic discontent Republicans insist that Trump’s tax cuts and immigration crackdown will benefit Americans, and they are portraying Democratic candidates as left-wing radicals. But in his final public campaign appearance Monday, Trump barely touched on the economy and spent most of the time in a rambling talk about his problem-plagued renovation of Washington’s Reflecting Pool. Democratic US Senate candidate Chris Pappas speaks to members of the media after voting in the US midterm elections at Webster Elementary School in Manchester, New Hampshire, US, November 3. — Reuters “This is the last day before the midterm elections, the most important midterm I believe in our lifetime,” he said, 26 minutes into the speech, before quickly returning to talking about renovations. Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer branded it a “pathetic closing message.” Some Republican supporters remain confident. “We’re going to win. As a matter of fact, we’ve probably already won,” Texas military veteran Yvonne Clouser told AFP . But while Republicans hold a 53-47 Senate majority, the battlefield is extending into conservative states like Kansas, Texas, Iowa, Ohio and Alaska. Democrats must also defend competitive seats, including in Michigan, where a bitter internal dispute saw congresswoman Haley Stevens endorse Republican Mike Rogers rather than the Democratic nominee, Abdul El-Sayed. Decision Desk HQ’s final forecast forecasted 241 House seats for Democrats against 194 for Republicans, and a narrower 52-48 Democratic Senate majority. Disputed results? Polls can underestimate one party’s support, and Republicans hope their voters turn out in force on Election Day. More than 57 million Americans had already voted early before Tuesday, indicating the high energy. A voter poses with their “I Voted” sticker after submitting their ballot at a polling place in the Marine on St Croix City Hall on November 3, 2026 in Marine on St Croix, Minnesota. — AFP The campaign has attracted more than $11 billion in political advertising, while billionaire Trump ally Elon Musk has poured hundreds of millions of dollars into Republican political efforts. As soon as polls close, concerns will mount over whether results will be accepted by the Republicans. Trump, who tried to overturn his 2020 election defeat, has repeatedly alleged widespread voter fraud and accused Democrats — with no evidence — of cheating. The Justice Department, run by a close Trump ally, has already sued to potentially block certification of Alaska’s Senate race if Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan narrowly loses, although a court ruled against the effort on the eve of the election. And the Supreme Court rejected on Monday an emergency bid to force California to set aside the mail-in ballots of more than 20,000 people on the grounds they may not be American citizens. Trump, who will watch the midterms results at the White House on Tuesday night, signalled that if he does lose control of Congress he could simply defy Democrats. “I veto everything,” he told a podcast on Monday, although he said he might strike deals with Democrats eventually.

items.title: Ten new scholars join Drive to Inspire – Africa, continuing scholars receive laptops
items.description: Ten new tertiary students have joined the Drive to Inspire – Africa LBG (DTI-A) scholarship programme, while some continuing scholars have received laptops to support their academic work. The awards were presented at a scholarship ceremony in Accra on October 30, 2026, organised by DTI-A in partnership with the Sanjeev Mansotra Foundation (SMF). The new beneficiaries were selected through a competitive process based on academic excellence and financial need. Their scholarships were funded by SMF under a partnership announced on April 21, 2026. The latest cohort marks the first time male tertiary students have been admitted to the DTI-A scholarship programme, which previously supported young women. The additional 10 beneficiaries bring the total number of scholarships awarded under the SMF-DTI-A partnership to 20. Speaking at the ceremony, DTI-A Founder, Nana Adjoa Hackman, recalled the uncertainty surrounding the scholarship initiative when the organisation was established, particularly concerns about receiving more applications than it had the resources to support. She said the programme, launched in late 2024 with 17 young women enrolled in 11 tertiary institutions across Ghana, had since grown to 70 scholars. Ms Hackman credited partners such as the Sanjeev Mansotra Foundation for helping expand the initiative and urged beneficiaries to regard every opportunity as an investment in their future. Founder of the Sanjeev Mansotra Foundation and Chairman of Planet One Group, Sanjeev Mansotra, said the partnership reflected his organisation’s commitment to expanding access to education. “We are pleased with the collaboration with DTI-A as our partner for the scholarship programme. Our vision for Ghana is that every capable child, regardless of circumstance, can pursue their ambitions and return value to the community. The scholars of today will be the innovators, educators and leaders who build the Ghana of tomorrow,” he said. He added that educating girls had wider benefits for families, communities and the country. Representing SMF, its Group Company Secretary and Head of Corporate Affairs, Ganesh Umashankar, stressed the importance of ensuring that no one was left behind in the pursuit of education. He encouraged the beneficiaries to make the most of the support and use their education to create positive change in their communities. One of the scholarship recipients, Rosemary Ofori, a University of Ghana student pursuing a Bachelor of Arts degree in Political Science, Geography and French, thanked DTI-A and SMF for the support. She pledged to make the most of the opportunity. The partnership also provides scholarship beneficiaries with a potential pathway to study at the University of Stirling’s Ras Al Khaimah campus in the United Arab Emirates, subject to meeting the university’s entry requirements and securing admission.

items.title: ASEC backs Ghana’s 2,000mw nuclear power plan, urges stronger maintenance culture
items.description: The Africa Sustainable Energy Centre (ASEC) has welcomed Ghana’s reported cooperation with Russia to develop a 2,000-megawatt nuclear power plant following President John Mahama’s recent visit to the country. The Centre says the proposed facility could strengthen energy security, diversify electricity generation and support industrialisation. ASEC Executive Director, Ing. Justice Ohene-Akoto, says nuclear power could provide reliable electricity to complement the country’s existing hydroelectric and thermal generation. However, he insists the project must form part of a broader energy diversification strategy. “Nuclear power should complement, not replace, Ghana’s renewable energy ambitions. We must continue to invest in solar, wind and battery storage to build a resilient and sustainable electricity system,” he said. ASEC says Ghana’s considerable solar potential remains underutilised and presents opportunities for increased investment in renewable energy. The Centre is also calling for greater involvement of Ghanaian universities, research institutions and engineering companies in the proposed nuclear programme to promote technology transfer, skills development and local industrial capacity. On maintenance, ASEC is warning that Ghana must address weaknesses in its existing energy infrastructure before embarking on the nuclear project. The Centre says the country must move away from reactive maintenance towards preventive and predictive systems, supported by adequate funding, skilled personnel and institutional accountability. Ing. Ohene-Akoto says Ghana’s maintenance culture must improve to support its nuclear ambition. “We cannot aspire to operate a world-class nuclear power facility while maintaining a third-class maintenance culture. Nuclear power requires uncompromising standards of preventive maintenance, operational discipline and safety,” he said. ASEC is urging government to strengthen maintenance across generation facilities, transmission networks, substations and distribution infrastructure to improve reliability. The Centre is also calling for independent nuclear regulation, compliance with International Atomic Energy Agency standards, emergency preparedness and comprehensive radioactive waste management. It further wants government to ensure transparent financing and procurement, assess the long-term cost of the project and strengthen transmission infrastructure to accommodate the additional generation capacity. ASEC says Ghana’s nuclear ambition presents an opportunity to strengthen energy security and advance technological development. However, Ing. Ohene-Akoto says the country must ensure that its ambitions are matched by adequate preparation and accountability. “Safety, maintenance culture, renewable energy development and the national economic interest must remain non-negotiable,” he said. The Centre has urged government to develop an integrated energy roadmap that balances nuclear and renewable energy investments while prioritising safety, local capacity development and long-term sustainability.

items.title: Algérie : l'inscription de villes au registre de l'ALECSO dénoncée par le mouvement kabyle
items.description: L’inscription par l’Algérie des villes de Mila et de Béjaïa au registre du patrimoine de l’Observatoire du patrimoine architectural et urbain dans les pays arabes, relevant de l'Organisation arabe pour l’éducation, la culture et les sciences (ALECSO), a suscité une vive contestation de la part du Mouvement pour l'autodétermination de la Kabylie (MAK) et du Gouvernement provisoire kabyle en exil (Anavad). Par la voix de son président, Ferhat Mehenni, l'organisation accuse Alger de vouloir déposséder la Kabylie de son héritage historique en le rattachant au monde arabe, tout en induisant en erreur les institutions chargées de la protection du patrimoine. Dans une lettre adressée à la Ligue des États arabes ainsi qu'à l’UNESCO, Ferhat Mehenni reproche aux autorités algériennes de poursuivre les politiques d'arabisation menées depuis l'indépendance et de chercher à effacer l'identité kabyle et amazighe. Le leader du MAK s'interroge sur les critères historiques et scientifiques ayant présidé au choix d'intégrer Béjaïa, Mila ainsi que Nedroma dans le registre du patrimoine arabe, estimant que cette démarche met en jeu la crédibilité des classements patrimoniaux internationaux en occultant l'origine et la diversité des civilisations concernées. Le responsable souligne que Mila et Béjaïa sont des cités kabyles, tandis que Nedroma présente des racines marocaines, toutes profondément ancrées dans la civilisation amazighe. S'il précise ne pas nier les apports et interactions avec le monde arabe au fil des siècles, le texte insiste sur le fait que la reconnaissance de ces influences ne saurait autoriser la négation de l'identité première de ces villes ni transformer un héritage amazigh en un patrimoine exclusivement arabe, qualifiant ce procédé d' « usurpation culturelle » et de « falsification de l'histoire ». Rappelant que la Kabylie a proclamé son indépendance le 14 décembre 2025, Ferhat Mehenni dénonce une logique de « colonisation culturelle » et affirme la détermination de la région à faire valoir son identité auprès des institutions internationales. L'organisation kabyle invite la Ligue arabe à veiller à ce que les inscriptions à ses registres ne soient pas interprétées comme une appropriation de l'histoire de peuples ne se définissant pas comme arabes, tout en exigeant des autorités algériennes la publication des fondements documentaires, scientifiques et culturels ayant justifié cette démarche. The post Algérie : l'inscription de villes au registre de l'ALECSO dénoncée par le mouvement kabyle appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: ‘Start small and alone’ – Agribusiness expert warns young people against business partnerships with friends
items.description: Young people hoping to venture into agribusiness have been advised to consider starting their businesses independently on a small scale rather than immediately entering partnerships with friends, particularly when they lack clear arrangements for sharing responsibilities, managing losses and accounting for investments. Executive Director of the Centre for Climate Change & Food Security (CCCFS) and Director of the West African Journalists for Environment, Science, Health and Agriculture (WAJESHA), Engr. Mahmud Mohammed-Nurudeen, says business partnerships, although potentially beneficial, can strain friendships when partners do not have equal access to information about the operations and financial performance of their businesses. He gave the advice while responding to a question about starting a business and the challenges of entering partnerships during an Agribusiness Incubation Workshop organised by residents of Jacob Jonas Nortey Hall at Valley View University’s Oyibi campus. “If you want to keep your relationship and integrity, do not go into agribusiness partnership with your friends. Start alone in a small way and grow,” he advised. According to him, the problem with some partnerships is that one person ends up carrying most of the responsibility while the others remain largely disconnected from the daily operations of the business. He said this arrangement could create suspicion, particularly when the person managing the business begins reporting losses, unexpected expenditure or operational challenges that the other partners have not personally witnessed. “If you are there alone, they won’t believe the stories you tell them,” he cautioned. Engr. Mohammed-Nurudeen explained that agribusinesses, especially poultry farms, are exposed to several uncertainties, including disease outbreaks, fluctuating production costs, market conditions and unfavourable weather. He said partners must therefore be actively involved and regularly informed about developments on the farm, including profits, losses, operational difficulties and the effects of adverse weather conditions. “Ensure everyone is involved. Let everyone know what happens on the farm, the gains, losses, the bad weather, etc.,” he stressed. When friendship meets business Drawing on his experience training and guiding young people interested in agribusiness, the climate and agricultural development expert said he had witnessed partnerships collapse because of mistrust and disagreements over money. He cited cases involving graduates he had trained who ventured into poultry production together but eventually fell out and abandoned their businesses because each partner suspected the others of cheating. “I know graduates I trained who went into poultry business but later fought and dispersed because each thought they were being cheated,” he recounted. He warned that financial disagreements between friends could extend beyond the business and damage relationships that had existed for years. In some instances, he said, a friend who feels cheated over an unpaid investment could resort to publicly accusing the other partner on social media, further complicating an already difficult situation. For him, the potential consequences make it important for young entrepreneurs to carefully consider the implications of mixing friendship with financial commitments. Partnerships are not entirely discouraged Although he recommends starting independently, Engr. Mohammed-Nurudeen clarified that he was not opposed to business partnerships. Rather, he believes partnerships are more appropriate when an entrepreneur has established a business, understood its operational demands and reached a stage where additional investment, expertise or resources are needed to expand. “Partnership can come when you want to expand,” he said. His advice forms part of continued message to young people that agribusiness requires entrepreneurs to identify opportunities, understand the market, build useful relationships and develop the discipline needed to manage their businesses. At the same workshop, he had urged young people not to wait until they accumulated substantial start-up capital before exploring opportunities across the agricultural value chain, arguing that identifying the right people and building networks could be just as important as money. The workshop, held under the theme “Developing the Anti-Fragile Mindset: Agribusiness as a Catalyst,” explored opportunities for young people to establish sustainable businesses within the agricultural sector. For aspiring entrepreneurs, he says starting small can be a deliberate way of protecting relationships, maintaining accountability and building a business strong enough to accommodate partnerships in the future.

items.title: Any staff caught conniving with service providers to rob NHIS subscribers will be dismissed and prosecuted – NHIA CEO
items.description: The Chief Executive Officer of the National Health Insurance Authority (NHIA), Dr. Victor Bampoe, has warned that any staff of the Authority caught conniving with service providers to defraud National Health Insurance Scheme subscribers will face outright dismissal and prosecution. He said the Authority will not tolerate internal collusion that undermines the sustainability of the scheme. Dr. Bampoe described the continued cases of illegal out-of-pocket payments charged to NHIS members at health facilities, a practice he said defeats the entire purpose of the health insurance scheme. He made the statement during the commissioning of a new NHIS District Office complex at Ejura in the Ashanti Region, aimed at improving access to services in the area. According to him, the government has invested heavily in the scheme more than ever before, ensuring prompt payment of claims to credentialed health facilities, and it is worrying that patients are still being made to pay. He questioned the justification for facilities to charge clients for services that are fully covered under the NHIS benefits package. “I have never seen the country invest so much in the National Health Insurance Scheme. I am saddened and worried that after all this money being paid to the health facility, they tell the people seeking their services that certain services are not covered by the NHIS. Where does this leave us?” Dr. Bampoe said. He warned that any NHIA staff found complicit in such illegal payments will be dealt with decisively. “I have been put in charge of the NHIS, so I am telling you that if found complicit in this, I will send you straight home plus whatever sanction and prosecution. Our brothers in the health facilities, we have the right to sanction you, and my Regional Director is aware,” he cautioned. Dr. Bampoe assured members of the public that the Authority is strengthening its monitoring and enforcement systems to protect subscribers and preserve public confidence in the scheme.

items.title: Sanjeev Mansotra Foundation awards 10 more scholarships to African students under Drive to Inspire partnership
items.description: The Sanjeev Mansotra Foundation (SMF) has awarded 10 additional scholarships to young Africans under its partnership with Drive to Inspire – Africa LBG (DTI-A), bringing the total number of beneficiaries under the initiative to 20. The scholarships were presented at an award ceremony in Accra on October 30, 2026. The latest cohort is the first under the partnership to include male beneficiaries, marking an expansion of the programme’s support for both young men and women pursuing higher education. The Foundation’s Founder and Chairman of Planet One Group, Sanjeev Mansotra, said investing in young people’s education was essential to developing future leaders and contributing to national growth. “Every capable child, regardless of circumstance, can pursue their ambitions and return value to the community. The scholars of today will be the innovators, educators and leaders who build the Ghana of tomorrow,” he said. Representing SMF, the Group Company Secretary and Head of Corporate Affairs, Ganesh Umashankar, said the latest awards reflected the Foundation’s belief that no one should be excluded from opportunities to pursue education. He explained that the Foundation had sought a suitable partner to extend its support to both male and female students and found DTI-A aligned with its objectives. Mr Umashankar encouraged the beneficiaries to take advantage of the opportunity and use their education to contribute meaningfully to their communities. The latest awards follow an initial batch of 10 scholarships presented in April 2026, bringing the total number awarded through the partnership to 20. DTI-A Founder, Nana Adjoa Hackman, credited partners such as the Sanjeev Mansotra Foundation with helping expand the scholarship initiative. She said the programme had grown from 17 scholars at its inception to 70 beneficiaries. One of the new beneficiaries, Rosemary Ofori, a University of Ghana student pursuing a Bachelor of Arts degree in Political Science, Geography and French, expressed appreciation to the two organisations for the support. She pledged to make the most of the opportunity. The partnership also provides a potential pathway for DTI-A scholars to pursue further studies at the University of Stirling’s Ras Al Khaimah campus in the United Arab Emirates, subject to meeting the university’s entry requirements and securing admission. The Sanjeev Mansotra Foundation is a philanthropic organisation established by Planet One Group Chairman Sanjeev Mansotra as a voluntary social responsibility initiative. Its work focuses on education, healthcare and sustainable development, with programmes in Ghana, Guinea, Togo, Sierra Leone and India, among other countries.

items.title: Islamabad ATC grants bail to Imaan, Hadi in police altercation case
items.description: ISLAMABAD: An anti-terrorism court (ATC) in Islamabad on Tuesday granted bail to lawyer Imaan Mazari and her husband, Hadi Ali Chattha, in a case registered against them for allegedly blocking a road outside the National Press Club and engaging in an altercation with police. ATC Judge Abual Hasnat Muhammad Zulqarnain announced the decision after hearing the bail applications. The police also produced the case record before the court during the proceedings. When defence counsel Riasat Ali Azad informed the court that the record had been received that day, the judge remarked that he would have shown the police the consequences of failing to produce it on Tuesday. The judge then asked the applicants if they had anything to say before announcing that their bail applications had been accepted. The court granted bail to both accused against surety bonds of Rs5,000 each. The judge also said he would examine the matter regarding the show-cause notice issued to the police over the delay in producing the case record. Last week, an ATC sentenced Imaan and Hadi to 10 years in prison each in the security breach case. The court also handed down one-year sentences and imposed fines of Rs50,000 each under Section 186 (obstructing a public servant in the discharge of public functions) of the Pakistan Penal Code (PPC). They were also sentenced to two years each under Section 353 (assault or criminal force to deter a public servant from discharging his duty) of the PPC. Jailed, sentenced, re-arrested The couple has been in jail since their arrest on Jan 23 in a case registered against them for protesting outside the IHC and allegedly manhandling the IHC Bar Association president. The arrest prompted criticism by rights bodies, politicians and journalists, who stressed the couple’s right to a fair trial. Just a day later, a sessions court sentenced them to 17 years on multiple charges under the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act in the controversial social media posts case. The convictions were widely condemned by lawyers and United Nations (UN) experts . On September 17, following months of litigation before the courts , the SC suspended their sentences in the case. The SC ordered their release pending the IHC’s final verdict on their appeals against the trial court’s decision. However, the reprieve was short-lived as hours later, Islamabad police arrested the couple again in connection with the security breach case. The case was registered at the federal capital’s Kohsar police station on March 22 last year on the complaint of City Magistrate Ghulam Murtaza Chandio.

items.title: Police investigate Spanish striker’s death after on-pitch collision with goalkeeper
items.description: Spain’s National Police have launched an investigation into the death of CD Tenerife striker Jesús de Miguel following his collision with FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono, with the case now under judicial supervision. Sources at the provincial police headquarters confirmed the development to AFP. De Miguel, 30, died at Nuestra Señora de La Candelaria Hospital, hours after sustaining serious injuries in a collision with Owono during Monday’s match at the Heliodoro Rodríguez López Stadium. “Broken with pain, with a lump in our throat and unable to believe this is real, CD Tenerife announces the tragic death, at 8:00 am (0700 GMT), of Jesus de Miguel Alameda,” his club Tenerife said in a statement. “No words can ease the pain, nothing can lessen this great feeling of sadness. Our thoughts are with the family, his close friends and Tenerife fans, who today are grieving over this terrible news.” The incident occurred in second-half stoppage time, with the score tied at 2-2, as the Tenerife striker chased an aerial ball beyond the halfway line. Spanish media said that De Miguel suffered a cardiac arrest and was resuscitated. The player was taken to hospital and placed in intensive care, with Tenerife later saying that De Miguel’s condition had “worsened neurologically”, before his death. The post Police investigate Spanish striker’s death after on-pitch collision with goalkeeper appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Tuberculose pédiatrique en Guinée : le PNLT et MSF renforcent les capacités des acteurs de santé de 33 préfectures pour mieux dépister les enfants
items.description: Mamou, Guinée – Les 20 et 21 octobre dernier, 33 points focaux tuberculose des préfectures du pays, aux côtés d'une dizaine de médecins exerçant en pédiatrie ou responsables de services pédiatriques, se sont retrouvés à Mamou autour d'un objectif commun : mieux repérer, diagnostiquer et prendre en charge la tuberculose chez les enfants. Organisée par le Programme National de Lutte contre la Tuberculose (PNLT), avec l'appui technique et financier de Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF), cette formation marque une nouvelle étape dans le renforcement durable des capacités du système de santé guinéen. La tuberculose demeure l'une des maladies infectieuses les plus meurtrières dans le monde. En Guinée, selon les estimations de l'Organisation mondiale de la Santé, près de 26 000 personnes devraient être diagnostiquées chaque année. Pourtant, environ 20 000 cas seulement ont été notifiés en 2025, laissant supposer plusieurs milliers de cas encore non détectés au sein des communautés. Chez les enfants, le défi est encore plus important. Alors qu'ils devraient représenter entre 10 et 15 % des cas diagnostiqués, la tuberculose pédiatrique ne représente aujourd'hui qu'environ 6 à 7 % des cas notifiés dans le pays. « La tuberculose pédiatrique présente les mêmes défis que la tuberculose de façon générale, mais avec des difficultés supplémentaires liées au diagnostic. Aujourd'hui, alors que les enfants devraient représenter au moins 10 % des cas dépistés, nous sommes encore autour de 6 %. Nous faisons d'importants efforts avec l'appui de nos partenaires pour combler cet écart et atteindre les objectifs fixés. » Dr Adama Camara, Coordinateur national du PNLT Pour inverser cette tendance, les participants ont été formés aux nouvelles recommandations de l'Organisation mondiale de la Santé, désormais intégrées dans le guide national de prise en charge de la tuberculose pédiatrique. Ils ont notamment travaillé sur les nouveaux algorithmes de dépistage, les méthodes de diagnostiques actualisées, l'interprétation de la radiographie thoracique, les traitements préventifs ainsi que la prise en charge des enfants exposés ou atteints de tuberculose. Cette initiative s'inscrit dans la continuité des efforts engagés ces dernières années pour améliorer la détection précoce de la tuberculose chez l'enfant en Guinée, notamment à travers le projet TACTiC. Au-delà du renforcement des connaissances individuelles, l'ambition est de doter durablement le système de santé guinéen d'outils, de compétences et d'approches éprouvées permettant au Programme national de poursuivre et d'amplifier les progrès réalisés. « Notre objectif n'est pas simplement d'organiser une formation supplémentaire. Nous voulons contribuer à laisser derrière nous des compétences, des outils pratiques et des capacités nationales que le PNLT pourra continuer à utiliser et à développer pour renforcer la lutte contre la tuberculose pédiatrique dans tout le pays. » Hanatou Tanko, cheffe du projet VIH-Tuberculose de MSF en Guinée L'une des principales innovations présentées durant l'atelier concerne l'utilisation des nouveaux algorithmes de dépistage A et B, développés pour faciliter le diagnostic précoce de la tuberculose chez les enfants, y compris dans les zones où les moyens diagnostiques restent limités. Selon la Dre Angéline Doré, formatrice principale de l'atelier, ces outils répondent à une réalité quotidienne des soignants en Guinée. « La particularité de ces algorithmes est qu'ils permettent de diagnostiquer précocement la tuberculose chez les enfants, y compris dans des contextes où l'accès à la radiographie est limité. Avec l'algorithme B, les résultats de radiographie ou d'autres examens ne sont pas toujours nécessaires. À partir des signes cliniques et des symptômes observés chez les enfants de moins de dix ans, les soignants peuvent déjà orienter leur diagnostic et référer rapidement les patients vers les structures appropriées. » Durant la formation, les participants ont travaillé à partir d'études de cas inspirées de situations réelles rencontrées sur le terrain. « Nous avons privilégié une approche très pratique. Les participants ont travaillé en groupe sur différents scénarios cliniques afin d'apprendre à utiliser concrètement ces nouveaux outils de diagnostic. L'objectif était qu'ils repartent avec des compétences immédiatement applicables dans leurs structures de santé. » Dr Angéline Doré Présent durant la formation, le Coordinateur national du PNLT a également rappelé que le renforcement des compétences des acteurs de terrain reste l'un des leviers essentiels pour améliorer le dépistage. « Les défis existent à plusieurs niveaux. Il faut poursuivre la sensibilisation des familles, renforcer l'implication communautaire, accompagner les agents de santé et continuer à former les pédiatres à la prise en charge de la tuberculose chez l'enfant. Cette formation organisée à Mamou s'inscrit pleinement dans cette dynamique. » Dr Adama Camara Les 33 participants réunis à Mamou ont désormais vocation à devenir des personnes ressources dans leurs préfectures respectives. À leur retour, ils auront la responsabilité de partager les connaissances acquises avec leurs collègues et d'accompagner la mise en œuvre des nouvelles approches diagnostiques dans les structures sanitaires locales. Pour le PNLT, l'appui de MSF continue de jouer un rôle important dans cette dynamique de renforcement des capacités. « Nous apprécions fortement l'accompagnement de MSF. Au-delà de son soutien historique à la prise en charge des patients, son engagement dans la formation des professionnels de santé nous aide à renforcer durablement notre capacité à détecter et prendre en charge la tuberculose chez les enfants. » Dr Adama Camara Pour la Dre Angéline Doré, le succès de cette formation se mesurera dans les mois à venir à travers une amélioration du dépistage et de la notification des cas pédiatriques à travers le pays. « Le message principal adressé aux participants est simple : restituer les connaissances acquises, renforcer le dépistage et améliorer la notification des cas de tuberculose pédiatrique. C'est ainsi que nous pourrons progressivement réduire les cas manqués et offrir une meilleure prise en charge aux enfants. » À travers cet accompagnement technique, MSF contribue aux efforts nationaux de lutte contre la tuberculose. Derrière les algorithmes, les formations et les outils diagnostiques, l’enjeu est avant tout humain : permettre à davantage d'enfants d'être dépistés à temps, d'accéder rapidement au traitement et de grandir en meilleure santé. Par Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) Guinée

items.title: Motrio lance un radiateur « Made in Algeria » pour les voitures Renault
items.description: Renault Algérie a annoncé, ce mardi 3 novembre, le lancement d’un nouveau radiateur de la marque Motrio, fabriqué localement en partenariat avec FB Radiateur. Les radiateurs Motrio « Made in Algeria » seront progressivement commercialisés à travers le réseauagréé de la marque spécialisée dans l’après-vente automobile du groupe Renault, à partir de ce mois de novembre 2026. « Ce nouveau produit a été développé dans le respect des exigences de qualité, de performance et de durabilité du Groupe Renault. Ce partenariat illustre également la capacité des industriels algériens à répondre aux standards des grands acteurs internationaux de l’industrie automobile », a indiqué Motrio dans un communiqué. Renault Algérie : un radiateur made « in algeria » pour ses véhicules Le directeur général de Renault Algérie, Hichem Nacer-Bey a déclaré que « le lancement du radiateur Motrio fabriqué en Algérie illustre notre engagement à renforcer continuellement notre offre après-vente afin de mieux répondre aux attentes de nos clients ». Grâce à ce partenariat avec FB Radiateur, « nous améliorons la disponibilité locale des pièces de rechange tout en garantissant des standards de qualité conformes aux exigences du Groupe Renault », a-t-il ajouté. De son côté, le directeur général de FB Radiateur, Salah Eddine Bouali, a exprimé la fierté de son entreprise à mettre son savoir-faire industriel au « service de la marque Motrio. » « Cette collaboration avec Renault Algérie représente une reconnaissance de l’expertise développée par nos équipes et une opportunité de contribuer activement au renforcement de l’industrie automobile nationale », a-t-il dit. De nouvelles références, en plus des 500 déjà commercialisées, viendront prochainement enrichir son offre a Motrio en précisant qu’elle dispose de 150 garages répartis à travers le territoire national. La Sarl FB Radiateur, qui fait partie du groupe Bouali, est spécialisée dans les systèmes de refroidissement automobile. Son usine est implantée dans la zone d’activité d’Ain M’lila, dans la wilaya d’Oum El Bouaghi. L’article Motrio lance un radiateur « Made in Algeria » pour les voitures Renault est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Osun APC backtracks, renames ‘parallel’ list as parliamentary campaign committee
items.description: By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo Following protest from members and rejection of a parallel presidential campaign committee by the national leadership, the Osun State All Progressives Congress (APC) has renamed its earlier presidential/parliamentary campaign committee to just the parliamentary campaign committee. The Osun APC in statement signed by the Party Chairman on Monday had released a parallel presidential campaign committee list which has the Governorship candidate as its Director-General after the Presidential Campaign Council Coordinator, Governor Ademola Adeleke, had inaugurated a campaign committee in the state. However, three members of the State Executive Committee, Wole Adunola, State Publicity Secretary; Adesola Ayangbile, Welfare Officer; and Rasheed Adeniji, Asst. Organising Secretary, and Abiola Ololade, Ex-Officio, in a joint statement, rejected the list on the ground that it does not reflect due process and lacked inclusiveness. This reportedly led to the national leadership of the party rejecting the said campaign committee list. Meanwhile, the APC, in another statement issued by the party chairman, Tajudeen Lawal, on Tuesday, renamed the list as parliamentary campaign committee, retaining the party’s governorship candidate in the August 15 election as the Director-General. The statement attached to the list reads, “Following the inauguration of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council (PCC) by the national leader of our party and its presidential candidate, His Excellency, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, GCFR, on the 14th of October 2026 in Abuja, and the subsequent inauguration of the Osun State PCC by the Executive Governor of Osun State, His Excellency, Governor Ademola Nurudeen Jackson Adeleke, on the 22nd of October 2026, we consider it extremely important to therefore bolster the efforts of the PCC to deliver massive votes for the reelection of our President, His Excellency, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu (GCFR) in the forthcoming general elections.” “We have therefore carefully selected out All Progressives Congress (APC) leaders and members in Osun State to actualise our collective desire of ensuring a round victory for the President as well as our National and State Assembly candidates. “As a party, we are resolute to work in unison with every member of the State Presidential Campaign to deliver on our mandate as we muster concerted efforts to ensure victory for all the National and State Assemblies candidates of our great party,” it added. The post Osun APC backtracks, renames ‘parallel’ list as parliamentary campaign committee appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Kozah / Plans alimentaires territoriaux : Le rapport diagnostic de la région de la Kara validé
items.description: Kara, 3 nov. (ATOP) – Les acteurs du secteur agricole et alimentaire de la région de la Kara ont validé, le lundi 2 novembre à Kara, le rapport diagnostic territorial des systèmes agricoles et alimentaires. Ce document servira de base à l’élaboration des Plans alimentaires territoriaux (PAT) des communes de la région. Les Plans alimentaires territoriaux sont des outils destinés à orienter les politiques locales en matière de souveraineté alimentaire et de valorisation des ressources du territoire. Ils visent à mieux exploiter les potentialités agricoles et pastorales, à renforcer la résilience des populations et à améliorer l’accès à une alimentation suffisante et de qualité. L’atelier de validation a été organisé par l’ONG Gestion de l’environnement et valorisation des produits agropastoraux et forestiers (GEVAPAF), en collaboration avec son partenaire Acting for Life. Il s’inscrit dans le cadre du projet « Appui à la résilience des populations et à la cohésion intercommunautaire au niveau des territoires transfrontaliers (PARCIT) ». Ce projet est mis en œuvre au Bénin, au Burkina Faso et au Togo, avec le soutien technique et financier de l’Union européenne. Le rapport présente les forces, les faiblesses et les opportunités des principales filières agricoles de la région, notamment le maïs, le riz, le soja et le maraîchage. Les participants ont pris connaissance de son contenu puis analysé les résultats du diagnostic avant d’amender le document. Le représentant du directeur régional en charge de l’Agriculture, M. Pibosso Pitiki-Abalo, a rappelé que l’agriculture constitue un socle essentiel à la survie humaine et au développement local, tout en garantissant la sécurité alimentaire des communautés. Le coordonnateur du projet PARCIT, Batcha Essozinam, a souligné l’importance d’analyser les potentialités locales et de confronter les résultats du diagnostic aux réalités des différentes communes. Il a exhorté les acteurs à traduire les conclusions du diagnostic en actions concrètes pour améliorer les conditions de vie des populations et renforcer leur résilience. Le représentant du maire de la commune Kozah 1, M. Kpatcha Aklesso a pris part à l’activité. ATOP/SG/AO/BV

items.title: Financing gaps threaten growth of Ghana’s electric two-wheeler industry – GCCE
items.description: The Ghana Chamber of Clean Energy (GCCE) has identified seven major financing constraints affecting businesses in Ghana’s electric two-wheeler industry, warning that the challenges could limit the sector’s growth. The concerns were outlined at a stakeholder consultative workshop organised by GCCE in partnership with the William Davidson Institute (WDI) at the University of Michigan in Accra on Tuesday, October 27, 2026. The workshop brought together electric two-wheeler manufacturers, assemblers, retailers, financial institutions and other industry stakeholders to examine financing barriers and explore ways to improve access to capital. A research team working with the two organisations presented seven preliminary financing gaps identified through the study. These include the limited implementation of announced import duty waivers for electric two-wheeler businesses and difficulties transitioning from grant funding to follow-on investment. Other challenges identified were companies relying on their own balance sheets to finance riders, limited access to affordable local-currency loans and lending requirements that early-stage businesses struggle to meet. The research also highlighted a mismatch between the asset-light business models preferred by equity investors and the financing needs of electric two-wheeler companies. Information and expectation gaps between businesses and capital providers were identified as another constraint. Delivering the opening remarks, GCCE’s Programmes and Outreach Manager, Emmanuella Biney, said addressing the challenges would require more than simply increasing the availability of funding. She said appropriate financing structures, stronger institutional collaboration and a supportive policy environment were also necessary to improve investor confidence and expand access to capital. “It also demands appropriate financing structures, stronger institutional collaboration, and an enabling environment that strengthens investor confidence, facilitates greater access to financing, and accelerates the adoption of electric two-wheelers in Ghana, contributing to cleaner air and a more sustainable transport sector,” she said. Ms Biney added that no single institution could resolve the challenges independently, stressing the need for coordinated action among government, financial institutions and industry players. Participants broke into groups to assess the seven preliminary findings, identify additional barriers and propose possible interventions. The discussions focused on strengthening collaboration between government, financial institutions, electric two-wheeler businesses and other industry stakeholders to improve financing opportunities and support the sector’s expansion. The findings and recommendations from the workshop will inform a joint public report to be developed by GCCE and WDI. The report is expected to guide the chamber’s engagement with government, financial institutions and industry stakeholders on policy and financing measures to address the barriers identified. Electric two-wheelers are increasingly being considered as part of Ghana’s transition to cleaner transport, with potential benefits for emissions reduction and employment. However, the financing challenges identified by the study could constrain the ability of businesses to expand their operations and reach more consumers.

items.title: GCB delivers strong quarter 3 2026 performance; profit rises to GH¢629.11m
items.description: GCB Bank PLC delivered another strong quarter, underpinned by robust balance sheet growth and high non-funded income. Total assets expanded by 35% year-on-year to GH¢67.62 billion, supported by 78% year-on-year growth in loans and advances, while deposits rose 34% year-on-year to GH¢50.78 billion, yielding a loan-to-deposit ratio of 51%. The Non-Performing Loan (NPL) ratio improved to 4.8% while the Capital Adequacy Ratio fell to 14.6%. Profit after tax (PAT) grew 39% year-on-year to GH¢629.11 million, above analysts’ estimates, lifting Return on Equity to 25%. Non-funded income rose 64% year-on-year, supporting growth and highlighting the growing contribution of non-interest revenue. However, interest income declined as the average lending rate dropped to 15.94% in August 2026 from 25.15% in August 2025. The rising operating expenses and lower interest rates weighed on the quarterly performance. Operating expenses increased 13% quarter-on-quarter to GH¢938.02 million, outpacing the 1% quarter-on-quarter rise in operating income to GH¢1.97 billion. The operating expenses rose largely due to a 19% quarter-on-quarter increase in personnel expenses, which deteriorated the cost-to-income ratio to 47.7% in quarter 3 2026 from 43% in quarter 2 2026. Loan portfolio drives balance sheet expansion Total assets increased by 35% year-on-year to GH¢67.62 billion, with loans and advances rising 78% year-on-year and 17% quarter-on-quarter to GH¢25.97 billion. Non-pledged trading assets also increased by 83% year-on-year to GH¢3.54 billion, while investment securities grew marginally by 2% year-on-year but declined 8% quarter-on-quarter to GH¢19.8 billion. The quarterly movements indicate a shift in the composition of the bank’s earning assets toward loan book growth and away from investment securities. Loan growth outpaces deposit mobilisation Deposits grew 34% year-on-year but contracted by 1.38% quarter-on-quarter to GH¢50.78 billion. Consequently, the loan-to-deposit ratio rose to 51% in quarter 3, 2026, from 43% in quarter 2 2026 and 39% in quarter 3 2025, reflecting faster loan growth relative to deposit mobilisation. While increased lending supports interest income generation, sustaining this trajectory will depend on the Bank’s ability to mobilise deposits and manage funding costs effectively.
