items.title: JI and Dar hold 'candid discussions' on fuel relief, agree to continue talks in coming days
items.description: The government and Jamaat-i-Islami (JI) on Tuesday held “candid discussions” on practical measures to provide relief to low-income citizens in petroleum prices. After a meeting with Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif last week, both sides agreed to form a bipartisan committee to expand the government’s ongoing fuel relief scheme in response to JI’s demands for the abolition of the petroleum levy. JI also warned of resuming its postponed march to Islamabad by mid-November if no relief was announced. Subsequently, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar on Tuesday held a meeting with a JI delegation, led by its Vice Emir Liaqat Baloch, to discuss petroleum prices in the country, according to the Dar-led Foreign Office (FO). “The two sides held candid discussions on practical measures to provide relief to the common man, with a specific focus on easing the economic burden on low-income citizens,” the FO statement said. Both sides agreed to continue their consultations over the coming days to formulate a way forward on energy pricing and public relief, it added. During the meeting, DPM Dar reiterated the “government’s commitment to prioritising public welfare and facilitating ordinary citizens amidst global economic challenges”, the statement said. He also emphasised that “sustained cross-party dialogue” remained key to addressing national economic challenges “effectively”. According to the statement, Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal, Adviser to Prime Minister Rana Sanaullah, Special Assistant to Prime Minister Tariq Bajwa, the finance secretary, and the Petroleum Division’s special secretary also attended the meeting from the government’s side. JI claims agreement on inclusion of 1,000cc cars in scheme After the meeting with the government’s team, the JI vice emir also addressed a press conference in Islamabad, according to a press release issued by the party. During his address, Baloch said that negotiations between the government and JI over the abolition of the petroleum levy and provision of relief to the public had entered their final stage. “Both sides have acknowledged that abolishing the petroleum levy is essential, while the government has also agreed to provide relief to the agricultural sector and owners of vehicles up to 1,000cc,” Baloch claimed. The ongoing relief scheme for owners of motorcycles, rickshaws and vehicles of up to 800cc was rolled out across the country on Sept 17. PM Shehbaz had announced the subsidies to ease the public’s burden amid rising fuel prices due to the Middle East situation. While describing the meeting as the final round of negotiations, Baloch said representatives of both sides will meet again tomorrow to discuss further progress. He said JI had presented six proposals to the government to provide relief to the people. “These included abolishing the petroleum levy, introducing a relief package, reducing public transport costs and extending relief to owners of vehicles above 800cc and the agricultural sector,” he said, noting that four key points were discussed today. The JI vice emir said both negotiating teams would prepare working papers on the gradual elimination of the levy and measures to provide relief to the public. “The government will complete its working paper today, while representatives of both sides will meet again tomorrow to discuss further progress,” Baloch said. He added that JI Emir Hafiz Naeemur Rehman would also review the draft agreement before announcing the party’s future course of action. He further disclosed that he had spoken by telephone with Rehman, who is currently in Turkiye, and briefed him on the progress of negotiations and sought his guidance. Baloch maintained that although the government had announced some relief measures, the ruling elite remained unwilling to surrender their privileges. He criticised the government for allowing oil refineries to earn excessive profits and said there was no solid justification for continuing the petroleum levy. Under a newly announced arrangement , oil refineries would contribute to the petroleum levy by bearing a monthly cumulative impact of Rs15 billion, according to the government. This would allow a Rs14.71 reduction in the petrol price on consumers’ end. Baloch affirmed that JI’s primary objective was to secure relief for the people, contending that the government has taken various relief measures due to his party’s negotiations. He further said that upon his return from Turkiye, Rehman would address JI workers nationwide online and announce the party’s future strategy. “Our protests will continue, and we will also engage in negotiations because we want to secure relief for the people,” Baloch said. “If this package does not come in the form of public convenience and substantial relief, Jamaat-i-Islami will fulfil its commitment to the people, and in mid-November, our protest march will set off from Multan towards Islamabad,” Baloch declared. “Our stance is very clear and unequivocal; we will also exercise the right to protest, but our protest will be peaceful, dignified, and aimed at securing relief for the people, as always.” JI protests so far The JI has been demanding for over two months that the Centre abolish petroleum levies, as fuel prices have skyrocketed due to conflicts in the Middle East since March. The Centre and JI had agreed to form committees in early September — when the latter had planned a nationwide strike — to recommend measures to reduce the levy. On Sept 20, the party launched a protest march towards Islamabad, warning that if the government failed to abolish the petroleum levy, the protest could turn into one to oust the government. On Sept 22, the JI emir said his party, whose convoy had reached Multan, was postponing its long march at the request of PM Shehbaz, who had assured the other side of a meeting to discuss the matter. When PM Shehbaz and Rehman finally met about a month later, they agreed to form a joint committee to recommend proposals for expanding the fuel relief scheme and for a phased reduction in the petroleum levy for the next budget.

items.title: Creatives must shape climate policies from the outset, not serve as last-minute amplifiers – GAYO
items.description: The Director of Operations and Programmes at the Green Africa Youth Organisation (GAYO), Betty Osei Bonsu Adjei, has called for the early involvement of creatives in climate initiatives, arguing that they should help shape decisions rather than be brought in at the final stages to promote them. She said artists, musicians, filmmakers and other cultural practitioners had the capacity to influence climate conversations through their creative approaches and understanding of audiences, but their contributions were often underutilised when they were excluded from the initial planning stages. Mrs Adjei made the remarks during the opening panel discussion at the Climate x Culture Summit 2026, held under the theme “Climate x Culture: Why Creativity Matters in the Climate Decade”. The summit was organised by CultureJoint Media in partnership with the Office of the Minister of State for Climate Change and Sustainability at the Presidency, under the overarching theme “Designing Sustainable Creative Experiences for Africa”. “Creatives are not last-minute amplifiers. They can use their creative ways and practices to help effectively elevate conversations around climate change. Hence whenever there’s such dicussions, be it researches, policy making among others, they should be included in the process,” the director said. She argued that climate programmes were often designed by policymakers, researchers and development organisations, with creatives brought on board towards the end to help communicate or promote decisions that had already been made. According to her, this approach limits the contribution of cultural practitioners, whose understanding of audiences and ability to communicate through compelling stories could help shape the design and delivery of climate interventions. She said involving creatives from the planning stage would allow their knowledge, experiences and storytelling approaches to inform how climate initiatives were developed and communicated to communities. Mrs Adjei, who doubles as the founder of B. Inspired with Stories from Africa ( B . ISA ) participated in the panel alongside Dr Enoch Bessah of the DIPPER Lab at the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST), Valerie Kplorm Nutakor of the Climate and Development Knowledge Network (CDKN), and musician and climate activist Okyeame Kwame. The discussion was moderated by Derick Ashilevi.

items.title: Cambriolage à la RTG2 : vers un congé technique pour les travailleurs avec les caméras numériques et équipements emportés
items.description: Un cambriolage d’une ampleur particulièrement préoccupante a été perpétré dans les locaux de la Radiodiffusion Télévision Guinéenne (RTG 2). Plusieurs équipements audiovisuels indispensables au fonctionnement de la chaîne ont été dérobés par des individus dont l’identité reste, pour l’heure, inconnue. Une enquête est en cours afin de faire la lumière sur cette intrusion. Selon les premiers témoignages recueillis sur place, les malfaiteurs auraient forcé l’accès à la régie avant de s’introduire à l’intérieur des installations. Ils auraient ensuite brisé une baie vitrée pour atteindre le grand plateau de la télévision, où ils ont méthodiquement emporté plusieurs équipements techniques. Interrogé sur les circonstances de cette opération, Oumar Le Bon Touré, responsable technique de la RTG 2, a dressé un inventaire provisoire du matériel disparu : « Les quatre caméras numériques, douze micros HF, un mélangeur vidéo, la commande des caméras robots ainsi qu'une mallette ont été emportés. Quant à la console, ils n'ont visiblement pas eu le temps de la transporter. Ils l'ont laissée dans le couloir », a-t-il expliqué, non sans annoncer un congé technique pour les travailleurs si rien n'est fait imminemment. D'après ses précisions, les faits auraient été découverts après un appel du responsable du matériel qui l'a informé d'un vol survenu dans les locaux de la chaîne. À son arrivée, il a constaté les dégâts occasionnés par les cambrioleurs. Le dispositif habituel de fonctionnement de la télévision pourrait également apporter quelques éléments de compréhension. Après le journal de 20 heures, les agents mettent généralement en place une programmation automatique destinée à assurer la diffusion des émissions préenregistrées durant toute la nuit. Les clés des installations sont ensuite déposées au poste de gendarmerie des environs, généralement entre 20h30 et 21 heures. Les locaux restent ainsi sans présence permanente jusqu'au lendemain matin. Pour l'heure, les circonstances exactes de cette intrusion demeurent inconnues. Les autorités compétentes ont été saisies et des investigations sont en cours pour identifier les auteurs de cet acte et retrouver les équipements dérobés. Au sein des travailleurs, visiblement embarrassés par l'ampleur des dégâts, un constat revient avec insistance : la maison se trouvait dans un sommeil profond depuis longtemps. Plusieurs semblent s'accorder sur un point : son réveil, ou du moins le regain d'attention porté à son fonctionnement, est à mettre à l'actif du ministre de la Communication, de l'Économie numérique et de l'Innovation, Fana Soumah. Un réveil qui intervient dans un contexte où les attentes autour de la modernisation et de la redynamisation de l'audiovisuel public restent particulièrement fortes. D'ailleurs, arrivé sur les lieux du cambriolage, le ministre Fana Soumah a préféré garder le silence alors que des journalistes s'apprêtaient à recueillir sa réaction. Face à l'ampleur des dégâts et à la gravité de cet acte, il n'a finalement pas souhaité faire de déclaration. Au-delà de la valeur matérielle des équipements emportés, ce cambriolage pose une question fondamentale : comment un patrimoine audiovisuel aussi stratégique a-t-il pu être aussi vulnérable ? Les investigations devront notamment permettre de déterminer les circonstances de cette intrusion, les éventuelles défaillances du dispositif de sécurité et les responsabilités éventuelles. Pour la RTG 2, l'heure est désormais à l'évaluation des pertes, à la sécurisation des installations et à la recherche des auteurs de ce cambriolage.

items.title: News fatigue pushing audiences towards lighter digital content – MFWA
items.description: The Programmes Manager of the Media Foundation for West Africa (MFWA), Kwaku Krobea, says growing fatigue with hard news and political discussions is driving some audiences towards lighter and more entertaining digital content. Speaking on Joy Prime’s Money Making Monday , Mr Krobea said the constant coverage of wars, deaths and political disagreements was leaving some people looking for content that offers a break from difficult news topics. He cited reports on the Russia-Ukraine war, tensions between the United States and Iran, and political debates involving the New Patriotic Party (NPP) and the National Democratic Congress (NDC) as examples of issues that could contribute to audience fatigue. “People get tired. And so then they want to consume certain forms of content,” he said. Mr Krobea described the trend as escapism, explaining that some audiences turn to comedy, skits, dance videos and other light-hearted content to take a break from the pressures of following current affairs. “People want to escape from all those tiring political conversations, so let’s take something that is light, maybe somebody dancing, a content creator creating jokes, a skit maker,” he added. He said the shift reflected changing audience preferences, with some people seeking entertainment alongside their consumption of news and other information. Mr Krobea also said the growing use of digital platforms was no longer limited to younger people. He noted that although younger audiences were initially quicker to adopt new technologies, more older people were becoming comfortable with smartphones and social media platforms such as TikTok. According to him, this was gradually narrowing the gap between younger and older audiences in the consumption of digital content.

items.title: 2027: Don’t stop at voting, hold Tinubu govt accountable — Egwu urges Nigerians
items.description: By Luminous Jannamike & Chidinma Chukwu ABUJA — As Nigeria approaches the 2027 general election, former Resident Electoral Commissioner, Prof. Sam Egwu, has urged Nigerians to look beyond casting their votes and hold the Tinubu administration accountable, warning that shrinking civic space, restrictions on media freedom and weak accountability are threatening the country’s democracy. He said citizens must not wait until election day to participate in governance but should remain engaged, question government policies and demand answers from elected officials. Egwu spoke at the 20th anniversary gala and lecture of the Resource Centre for Human Rights and Civic Education, CHRICED, in Abuja, where he delivered a lecture titled, ‘Reclaiming Civic Space: The Rule of Law, Democratic Accountability, and the Future of Citizens’ Participation in Nigeria.’ Describing civic space as the bedrock of democracy, the former INEC commissioner said its protection was essential to allowing citizens and civil society organisations to organise, participate in governance and express their views freely. “Civic space is very important to the construction of democracy. It is the bedrock of any open and democratic society. “Where civic space is open, citizens and civil society organisations are able to organise, participate and communicate without hindrance,” he said. Egwu said the enthusiasm that greeted Nigeria’s return to democratic rule in 1999 had gradually diminished amid growing concerns over democratic freedoms, despite constitutional provisions guaranteeing citizens’ rights. He also questioned the accountability surrounding major economic decisions of the Tinubu administration, including exchange rate unification, fuel subsidy removal, the new tax regime and electricity tariffs. “I would argue that even the policies introduced by the present administration raise serious questions about accountability to the Nigerian people. “These policies raise fundamental questions about how public decisions are made, the extent to which citizens’ interests are considered and the mechanisms through which the government accounts for the consequences of its decisions,” he said. Chairman of the occasion and CHRICED board member, Dr. Dayo Olaide, said protecting democracy required collective action beyond the work of civil society organisations. “Making democracy work is a collective responsibility that requires the commitment and participation of all of us. It starts with speaking up. It goes beyond simply going out to vote. We must also ensure that our votes count and that the will of the people is reflected in the outcome of elections,” he said. Olaide urged Nigerians to judge elections by what they deliver for citizens and their contribution to making democracy work. Earlier, CHRICED Executive Director, Comrade Ibrahim Zikirullahi, said the organisation was established 20 years ago to address citizens’ exclusion from governance and promote democratic accountability. He said its work had focused on civic education, electoral integrity, empowering women and young people, protecting vulnerable groups and improving access to public services. The organisation also unveiled two publications on civic engagement and its public interventions from 2020 to 2026 as part of the anniversary celebration, held under the theme, ‘20 Years of Voice and Justice: Empowering Citizens, Shaping Tomorrow.’ The post 2027: Don’t stop at voting, hold Tinubu govt accountable — Egwu urges Nigerians appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: 28 states approve State Police Bill as NASS moves to transmit to Tinubu
items.description: By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja The National Assembly has received approval from 28 State Houses of Assembly for the proposed constitutional amendment seeking to establish state police in Nigeria. The approval exceeds the constitutionally required threshold of 24 states, representing two-thirds of the 36 State Houses of Assembly, paving the way for the transmission of the bill to President Bola Tinubu for assent. The Clerk to the National Assembly, Kamoru Ogunlana, disclosed this in a statement on Tuesday, saying the reports received from the 28 state legislatures had been verified alongside their respective votes and proceedings. According to the statement, the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 (Sixth Alteration) Bill, which seeks to provide for the establishment of State Police Services and related matters, was transmitted to the 36 State Houses of Assembly on September 16, 2026, for consideration and approval. The state legislatures were initially given 30 days, ending October 15, to communicate their decisions to the National Assembly. However, Ogunlana said his office would continue to receive reports from the state assemblies until the bill is transmitted for presidential assent. He said, “Following the receipt and verification of the reports, the Office confirms that 28 State Houses of Assembly have approved the Bill. “This represents more than the constitutionally prescribed threshold of not less than two-thirds of the 36 State Houses of Assembly, equivalent to 24 States, as required under Section 9 of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999.” The clerk explained that the National Assembly had undertaken administrative verification of the reports and accompanying votes and proceedings to establish their authenticity and ensure that they accurately reflected the decisions taken by the respective state legislatures. He also clarified that Section 9 of the Constitution does not expressly prescribe a third reading for a Constitution Alteration Bill, unlike the procedure applicable to ordinary bills. items.title: Manifestations en France: Darmanin annonce quelque 5.000 gardes à vue, 329 incarcérations
items.description: Le ministre français de la Justice, Gérald Darmanin, a indiqué mardi qu’il y a eu 4.914 gardes à vue et 329 personnes incarcérées depuis le 17 octobre, premier acte des manifestations contre la vie chère. « Depuis ce 17 octobre, y a eu 4.914 gardes à vue, dont 70% sont des majeurs et 30% sont des mineurs, ce qui montre bien d’ailleurs que c’est un mouvement d’adultes, et pas le mouvement de continuité des lycéens », a fait valoir Darmanin. « Il y a eu 1.820 personnes qui ont été déférées avec des policiers ou des gendarmes, de la garde-à-vue jusqu’au tribunal pour être jugées par un juge correctionnel, avec 404 mesures d’emprisonnement et 329 incarcérations » , a poursuivi le garde des Sceaux, se félicitant d’une réponse pénale extrêmement forte. Le ministre de la Justice a en outre fait état de « profils extrêmement variés » parmi les personnes condamnées, notamment « selon le weekend de mobilisation » , avec « 95 % d’hommes et 5 % seulement de femmes ». « Deux tiers ont entre 18 et 25 ans, 70 % sont français et plus de 50 % n’avaient aucun antécédent judiciaire », a encore énuméré Gérald Darmanin. items.title: MFWA urges tech platforms to financially support media organisations
items.description: The Media Foundation for West Africa (MFWA) has called on technology companies to financially support media organisations whose content attracts audiences to their digital platforms. The Foundation’s Programmes Manager, Kwaku Krobea, said digital platforms benefit from journalism produced by traditional media organisations and should contribute to their financial sustainability. Speaking on Joy Prime’s Money Making Monday , Mr Krobea said technology companies must be held accountable for the value they derive from media content shared on their platforms. “Maybe the bigger conversation we should be having is, you know, the platform accountability, holding the platforms accountable to say … people are watching you because of our content,” he said. Mr Krobea said the traditional media advertising model was becoming increasingly difficult to sustain as advertisers shifted more of their spending to digital platforms. He explained that platforms such as YouTube and Facebook offer advertisers greater flexibility to target audiences based on demographics and interests, an advantage traditional media outlets do not provide to the same extent. “Frankly, that business model is failing. And there are no two ways about that,” he said. He noted that media organisations could also leverage their social media platforms to attract advertisers but maintained that this did not remove the responsibility of technology companies to recognise the value of the content that keeps users engaged. Mr Krobea cited Australia as an example of a country that had taken steps to address the imbalance between technology platforms and news publishers, adding that other countries were also drawing lessons from its approach. He, however, maintained that traditional media was not losing its relevance. Rather, he said media organisations must adapt to changing audience preferences and patterns of content consumption while exploring sustainable ways of operating in an increasingly digital media environment.

items.title: Ghana strengthens border surveillance amid Bundibugyo Ebola virus outbreak
items.description: Ghana has stepped up public health surveillance at its international airports, introducing enhanced screening and monitoring measures for travellers arriving from countries affected by an outbreak of Ebola Disease caused by the Bundibugyo virus. The measures, announced by the Ministry of Health through the Ghana Health Service (GHS), are aimed at preventing the possible importation and spread of the disease through international travel. In a statement issued on Tuesday, November 3, 2026, and signed by the Minister for Health, Kwabena Mintah Akandoh, MP, the Ministry said Ghana had not recorded any confirmed case of Ebola Disease but was taking precautionary steps to strengthen its preparedness. “To date, Ghana has not recorded a confirmed case of Ebola Disease. These measures are precautionary and will be reviewed as the situation evolves,” the statement said. The Ministry explained that the interventions were intended to “minimise the risk of Ebola being brought into Ghana and spreading through international travel”. A key component of the new arrangements is the monitoring of passengers arriving from countries with ongoing transmission for up to 21 days after their arrival in Ghana. “The Ghana Health Service will contact them for follow-up, and they must keep reachable contact details and report any symptoms immediately to the designated contact,” the statement said. The monitoring arrangement is expected to support the early identification of possible infections and ensure that travellers who develop symptoms receive prompt medical attention. Travellers to declare recent travel history Under the new arrangements, passengers travelling to Ghana will be required to complete a Health Declaration Form and truthfully disclose whether they have visited or transited through any Ebola-affected country within the previous 21 days. They must also declare any close contact with a suspected or confirmed Ebola patient, visits to a health facility managing Ebola cases, participation in funeral or burial rites involving a suspected case, and contact with the blood, body fluids or contaminated materials of an ill person. The Ministry has advised travellers experiencing symptoms associated with Ebola, including fever, severe weakness, headache, vomiting, diarrhoea, or unexplained bleeding or bruising, to postpone their journeys and seek immediate medical attention. It specifically advised that travellers with such symptoms “should postpone travel and seek medical attention immediately”. All passengers to undergo airport screening Upon arrival in Ghana, every passenger will undergo screening by Port Health officers. The process will include non-contact temperature checks, a review of completed Health Declaration Forms and travel histories, as well as additional questions about symptoms and possible exposure where necessary. Passengers identified as having symptoms suggestive of Ebola, recent travel from or through affected countries, or possible exposure to an infected person will be referred for immediate secondary assessment. According to the Ministry, such individuals will be taken to a designated area for temporary isolation and evaluation before being referred to a health facility where necessary. Hotels and conference venues to report guests The Ministry has also extended the public health measures to the hospitality sector, directing hotels, conference venues and similar establishments to report guests arriving from Ebola-affected countries to the nearest district health directorate of the Ghana Health Service. The statement said: “Hotels, conference venues and similar providers must report guests arriving from affected countries to the nearest district health directorate of the Ghana Health Service and keep records and contact details of all persons who access their facilities while such guests are hosted.” The requirement is expected to strengthen surveillance beyond the airports and assist health authorities in identifying individuals who may have come into contact with travellers under monitoring. Passengers warned against withholding information The Ministry has urged all arriving passengers to cooperate fully with Port Health officers, provide truthful information about their travel history and health status, and comply with screening instructions. It also urged passengers to “practise frequent hand hygiene” and immediately report any symptoms that develop during their flight or at the airport. The Ministry warned that “any passenger who knowingly gives false information, conceals symptoms or refuses to comply with screening will be subject to public health measures under Ghanaian law”. Measures follow Africa CDC ministerial meeting The Ministry said Ghana’s interventions were consistent with commitments made at a recent Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) ministerial meeting on Ebola. The meeting brought together all 55 African member states, including more than 40 ministers, to discuss preparedness and measures to prevent the spread of the disease across the continent. According to the statement, member states agreed to “implement the preparedness actions discussed, strengthen cross-border and border-point surveillance, and keep borders open while investing in measures to prevent transmission”. The commitments highlight the importance of regional cooperation in responding to public health threats while maintaining international travel and movement. Public urged to rely on official information Meanwhile, the Ministry has urged the public to rely on official information from the Ministry of Health and the Ghana Health Service and avoid spreading rumours about the outbreak. “The public is advised to rely on official information from the Ministry of Health and the GHS and to avoid spreading rumours,” the statement said. Anyone with health concerns has been advised to contact the nearest Port Health officer at the airport or visit the nearest health facility. The Ministry reiterated that Ghana had not recorded any confirmed case of Ebola Disease, stressing that the measures were precautionary and intended to strengthen the country’s capacity to detect and respond to any potential case.

items.title: Cambriolage à la RTG2 : les voleurs emportent plusieurs équipements techniques importants emportés dans un site pourtant sécurisé
items.description: Les installations de la RTG2, situées à Boulbinet, dans la commune de Kaloum, ont été la cible d'un cambriolage dans la nuit du lundi 2 au mardi 3 novembre 2026. Des individus non encore identifiés ont réussi à s'introduire dans les locaux de la chaîne publique pour emporter plusieurs équipements techniques de grande valeur, suscitant l'indignation et l'incompréhension de la direction générale. Les faits ont été découverts au petit matin par le personnel de la station. Présente sur les lieux, la directrice générale de la RTG Koloma, Makèmè Bamba, a dressé un premier bilan des dégâts. Selon ses explications, les assaillants ont notamment brisé la baie vitrée de la régie finale pour accéder à la salle du plateau. Le butin est particulièrement important. Les quatre caméras robots installées sur le plateau, ainsi qu'un amplificateur de son situé à proximité, ont été emportés. Les malfaiteurs ont également fait main basse sur d'autres équipements essentiels au fonctionnement technique de la chaîne, notamment le mélangeur vidéo et la console de commande des caméras. Certains matériels, trop encombrants ou abandonnés dans les couloirs, n'ont toutefois pas pu être emportés. Si la RTG2 a déjà enregistré des cas de vol par le passé, l'ampleur et le mode opératoire de cette nouvelle intrusion interpellent particulièrement la direction. Les individus ont en effet réussi à forcer plusieurs accès, notamment des baies vitrées et des portes blindées, dans un environnement pourtant réputé sécurisé et très fréquenté. « Je suis même étonnée […]. Qui peut oser venir prendre des équipements qui servent à toute la nation ? Parce que c'est tout le monde qui regarde la RTG2 », s'est indignée Makèmè Bamba, rappelant la vocation publique et l'importance de cette chaîne dans le paysage audiovisuel national. La directrice générale s'interroge également sur les motivations des auteurs de ce cambriolage. Selon elle, les équipements emportés ne permettent pas, à eux seuls, de mettre en place un studio de production autonome, d'autant que d'autres composantes techniques indispensables sont restées sur place. L'audace des cambrioleurs suscite d'autant plus de questions que le site abrite un camp militaire et dispose d'un poste d'accès armé, tenu par des gendarmes. À cela s'ajoute la présence régulière de travailleurs et d'autres usagers dans l'enceinte. Face à la gravité des faits, les services de gendarmerie déployés à l'entrée du site ont rapidement alerté les unités d'investigation compétentes. Des éléments de la police scientifique se sont rendus sur place dès les premières heures de la matinée afin de procéder aux constatations d'usage, notamment aux relevés d'indices et aux prises de vues photographiques, en vue de documenter les circonstances de l'intrusion. La direction générale de la RTG entend obtenir toute la lumière sur cette affaire. « Nous espérons que cette enquête ira jusqu'au bout afin qu'on découvre qui a voulu faire ça, et pourquoi », a conclu Makèmè Bamba, exprimant son souhait de voir les auteurs identifiés et leurs motivations établies.

items.title: CDS seeks civilian support, intelligence sharing to tackle terrorism
items.description: The Chief of Defence Staff, Gen. Olufemi Oluyede, has called for the support of civilians and host communities in the fight against terrorism. Oluyede made the call while speaking to newsmen on the sidelines of the 2026 Chief of Naval Staff (CNS) annual retreat on Tuesday in Abuja. According to Oluyede, there is a need for jointness and synergy among all key security stakeholders. Oluyede, whose philosophy for security lays heavy emphasis on synergy, said that jointness goes beyond inter-agency cooperation and also includes the civilians and communities. “It is important for us to continue to emphasise jointness because no single service can do the job alone, it requires a collective effort.” He said the armed forces are collectively doing their very best to make Nigeria safer, adding that what they require from Nigerians are support, prayers and intelligence reports. “If you see anything, you should tell us because everything we’re doing relies on intelligence, and for that, we need community support,” he said. He said the support provided by Nigerians would aid push the country forward on all fronts. He assured Nigerians that things would continue to get better. items.title: Terrorisme et blanchiment : 2 cellules démantelées et contrôle accru sur 7 casinos et 430 associations en 2026
items.description: Les services de sécurité marocains ont neutralisé deux cellules terroristes et mis en échec un projet d'attentat de grande envergure visant des infrastructures sensibles au cours de l'année 2026. Selon le rapport d'activité du ministère de l'Intérieur au titre de l'exercice budgétaire 2026, ces interventions traduisent la doctrine d'anticipation adoptée par le Royaume face à la persistance des menaces portées par l'organisation « Daech » et ses ramifications régionales, notamment dans la zone sahélo-saharienne et la Corne de l'Afrique. Démantèlements de cellules et projets d'attentats déjoués La première opération d'envergure, menée en mars 2026 en coordination avec les services de sécurité espagnols, a abouti au démantèlement d'une cellule affiliée à « Daech » active entre les deux pays. Cette intervention conjointe a permis l'arrestation à Tanger de deux individus soupçonnés d'assurer un soutien financier et logistique à ce réseau transfrontalier. En juillet 2026, un coup de filet majeur a permis de neutraliser une menace qualifiée d'extrêmement critique. Dix suspects ont été interpellés à travers sept villes marocaines. Les données du département de l'Intérieur établissent leur affiliation opérationnelle directe avec la branche sahélienne de « Daech ». Les personnes appréhendées projetaient de frapper des installations stratégiques du pays à l'aide d'un véhicule piégé. L'opération a également permis la saisie d'armes blanches et de plans détaillés destinés à la confection d'engins explosifs. Sur le front virtuel, les services compétents ont renforcé leur veille pour contrer la propagande extrémiste en ligne et l'émergence des « loups solitaires » . Ce dispositif numérique a rendu possible l'identification et l'interpellation de plusieurs individus radicalisés sur Internet, désamorçant des passages à l'acte individuels avant leur mise en œuvre. Cette vigilance opérationnelle s'est doublée d'un engagement continu dans la coopération multilatérale. Le ministère de l'Intérieur maintient sa participation aux programmes et conférences d'organismes spécialisés, notamment le Bureau des Nations unies contre le terrorisme (ONUCT), Interpol, le Forum mondial de lutte contre le terrorisme (GCTF), la Coalition internationale contre Daech et la Ligue des États arabes. Resserrement du contrôle sur les casinos et les jeux de hasard Parallèlement au volet opérationnel, le ministère de l'Intérieur a accentué ses contrôles sur les activités économiques vulnérables au blanchiment de capitaux et au financement du terrorisme, en coordination avec le ministère de l'Économie et des Finances. Au cours du mois d'avril 2026, des inspections ciblées ont été diligentées dans l'ensemble des sept casinos opérant au Maroc, implantés à Agadir (3 établissements), Marrakech (2), El Jadida (1) et Tanger (1). Les vérifications ont porté sur le respect des obligations légales de déclaration de soupçon, les procédures de vigilance à l'égard de la clientèle et l'identification précise des bénéficiaires effectifs des flux financiers. Ces contrôles ont été complétés par des cycles de formation destinés aux personnels des établissements de jeu, axés sur les standards nationaux et internationaux de détection des transactions atypiques. Cette campagne fait suite à une série de missions d'inspection conduites en janvier 2026 auprès des principaux opérateurs des jeux de hasard et de paris, à savoir la Loterie Nationale, la Société Royale d'Encouragement du Cheval (SOREC) et la Marocaine des Jeux et des Sports (MDJS), afin d'auditer leurs systèmes de veille et de transmission des déclarations suspectes. Encadrement et audit du tissu associatif Le dispositif de conformité s'est également étendu au milieu associatif pour prévenir le détournement de ses circuits à des fins illicites. Entre octobre 2025 et mars 2026, les autorités territoriales ont animé 1 708 rencontres de sensibilisation ayant touché 9 278 associations, les formant aux règles de traçabilité des ressources financières et aux risques d'exploitation clandestine de leurs fonds. En matière d'audit, 430 associations ont fait l'objet de contrôles directs et d'inspections ciblées en fonction de leur niveau d'exposition aux risques financiers. Ces initiatives répondent à l'application des recommandations du Groupe d'action financière (GAFI) et du GAFIMOAN (MENAFATF). Elles ont été appuyées par la rédaction d'un guide méthodologique officiel destiné à guider les organisations non gouvernementales dans la protection de leurs structures contre les circuits financiers illicites. The post Terrorisme et blanchiment : 2 cellules démantelées et contrôle accru sur 7 casinos et 430 associations en 2026 appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Le jour des midterms, Donald Trump souffle le chaud et le froid sur une reprise de la guerre contre l’Iran
items.description: a quelques heures des elections americaines de mi-mandat du 3 novembre, Donald Trump entretient l'incertitude sur une eventuelle reprise de la guerre contre l'Iran. Apres avoir multiplie les menaces de nouvelles frappes une fois l'examen passe, le president americain a brusquement reflechi a son discours lundi 2 novembre. Interroge sur la possibilite d'une offensive apres les midterms, il a repondu par la negative, affirmant qu'un accord avec Teheran restait envisageable. Ce revirement contraste avec ses declarations precedentes. La veille, Trump avait evoque la necessite de frapper a nouveau l'Iran si les negociations echouaient. Selon l'Associated Press, Washington a egalement averti plusieurs allies du Moyen-Orient de se preparer a une eventuelle campagne militaire apres les elections, ainsi qu'a des represailles iraniennes contre leurs infrastructures energetiques. Trump fait du Trump Sur le terrain, la pression americaine demeure. Selon le Washington Post, les forces americaines ont mene le 2 novembre des frappes sur l'île iranienne de Qeshm, dans le detroit d'Ormuz, presentees comme defensives. Des operations limitees qui temoignent de la persistance des hostilites, malgre les ouvertures diplomatiques. « La balle est desormais dans le camp americain », a declare le porte-parole de la diplomatie iranienne, Esmaïl Baghaï. L'Iran conditionne en effet la reouverture du detroit d'Ormuz a sept exigences adressees a Washington, notamment la levee du blocus naval, des sanctions economiques et le degel de ses avoirs. Teheran reclame egalement l'arret des operations militaires americaines contre son territoire et ses allies regionaux, dont le Hezbollah. Le chef de la diplomatie iranienne, Abbas Araghchi, propose une feuille de route sur sept jours, estimant que seule une solution negociee permettra de mettre fin au conflit. Pour Trump, l'enjeu est egalement interieur. La guerre et ses consequences sur les prix de l'energie pesent sur les electeurs americains. a la veille d'un examen decisif, le president cherche ainsi a maintenir la pression sur l'Iran sans exclure une sortie negociee du conflit.

items.title: Entertainer and enigma, Glenn Maxwell bows out as cricket's great what-if
items.description: Part entertainer, part enigma, Glenn Maxwell will go down in cricket folklore as the game’s great what-if a maverick shot-maker whose limited-overs wizardry never extended to red-ball cricket. Where many of his peers stuck to the batting manual, Maxwell rewrote it with his 360-degree stroke-play, which made field settings a nightmare for rival captains. It could not be risk-free, but Maxwell cared little as he pulled off reverse hits and cheeky scoops with a gum-chewing nonchalance. Fans expected spectacle whenever Maxwell walked out with the bat and, more often than not, he delivered it with his unorthodox shots. The definitive example came at the 2023 ODI World Cup. Chasing 292 against Afghanistan and with Australia reeling at 91-7, Maxwell conjured up an unforgettable 201 not out off 128 balls to complete a chase that had looked impossible. That sense of occasion was present from his Australia debut, an ODI against Afghanistan in 2012, and it studded his career. A two-time ODI World Cup winner, Maxwell also hit the winning runs in Australia’s maiden T20 World Cup triumph in 2021 under captain Aaron Finch. Fittingly, Finch fronted the tributes to Maxwell after a 286-match international career spanning 14 years. “Without doubt one of the most destructive players the game has ever seen and easily one of the most innovative of our generation,” Finch wrote on Instagram. “Some of the things you’ve done on a cricket field have been absolutely ridiculous. You’ve played innings that most of us could only dream of and produced some of the greatest moments this game has ever seen. You’ve changed the way the game is played and inspired so many along the way.” T20 royalty Maxwell’s value was always three-dimensional: explosive batting, savvy off-spin, and electric fielding that saved runs and snared jaw-dropping catches. It made him T20 royalty, especially in the Indian Premier League (IPL). Maxwell, 38, was an IPL millionaire at 25 and earned the nickname the “Big Show” after his first ODI series a moniker he resented. “At the start, I thought if I fight it, I’m going to have to live with it even more, so I tried to sort of ride with it,” Maxwell said in 2014. “I’m just trying to shake it off because it’s starting to go too far. “It’s not about what I’m about. I’m all about trying to entertain and…I just love being out there trying to hit balls for four and six.” That ability made him a crowd magnet evident in his 12.4 million followers across social media platforms. The long run was not without quiet chapters, and test cricket never became his stage. Maxwell played only seven tests between 2013 and 2017, scoring 339 runs at a modest average of 26. He took a mental health break from the sport in 2019 and recounts the episode in his autobiography in a candid assessment of the struggles that lay beneath his confident exterior.

items.title: VALCO breaks years of losses, posts US$1.3m profit on US$103.5m revenue
items.description: The Volta Aluminium Company Limited (VALCO) says it has returned to profitability, recording a profit of US$1.3 million on the back of US$103.5 million in revenue as of September 2026. Chief Executive Officer, Dr. Robert Makila Sambian, says the performance marks a significant turnaround after years of financial difficulties, following a strategic reset of the company. Speaking at the Ministry of Lands and Natural Resources’ Progress Report presentation, Dr. Sambian attributed the improvement to changes in human resource behaviour, operational reforms and a renewed focus on efficiency. He described the financial performance as a major milestone in efforts to restore the fortunes of the state-owned aluminium producer. Dr. Sambian said VALCO has also aligned its operations with President John Mahama’s 24-hour economy initiative, introducing a schedule of one job, four shifts and four workers to support round-the-clock production. He, however, acknowledged that more work and investment are required to sustain the gains and fully restore the company’s operations. He disclosed that VALCO is engaging strategic investors to mobilise the needed capital, with a long-term ambition of increasing production to 1.5 million metric tonnes over the next 10 years. The CEO says the company remains committed to strengthening its operations and reclaiming its position as a major player in Ghana’s industrial development.

items.title: Les États-Unis menacent de bannir l’Afrique du Sud et le Rwanda de l’AGOA dès 2027
items.description: L’administration américaine de Donald Trump a annoncé, le lundi 2 novembre 2026, son intention de retirer l’Afrique du Sud et le Rwanda du programme commercial AGOA, qui accorde des avantages douaniers aux pays africains exportant vers les États-Unis. Cette mesure, dont l’entrée en vigueur est prévue pour le 1er janvier 2027, est justifiée par Washington par le non-respect de plusieurs critères d’éligibilité par les deux pays. Le couperet pourrait bientôt tomber sur Pretoria et Kigali. À l’issue de son examen annuel des pays bénéficiaires de l’African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA), le représentant américain au Commerce (USTR), Jamieson Greer, a annoncé, dans un communiqué publié le lundi 2 novembre 2026, l’intention de l’administration Trump d’exclure l’Afrique du Sud et le Rwanda de ce dispositif préférentiel. Mis en place pour renforcer les échanges commerciaux entre les États-Unis et les pays africains, l’AGOA permet notamment aux États bénéficiaires d'exporter plusieurs catégories de produits vers le marché américain sans acquitter de droits de douane. Toutefois, cet avantage est soumis à des exigences liées, entre autres, à la gouvernance, à l’État de droit, aux droits humains et aux relations commerciales. Des griefs différents contre Pretoria et Kigali Pour justifier cette décision, Washington avance plusieurs reproches à l’encontre des deux pays. Concernant l’Afrique du Sud, les autorités américaines dénoncent des entraves aux échanges commerciaux, des problèmes de corruption ainsi que des préoccupations relatives à la sécurité nationale et à la politique étrangère sud-africaine. Les positions de Pretoria sur certaines questions internationales, notamment ses démarches judiciaires devant les instances internationales et les questions liées aux droits des Afrikaners, figurent également parmi les sujets de tension. Du côté du Rwanda, l’administration américaine évoque des restrictions commerciales, des insuffisances en matière d’État de droit et de respect des droits humains. Elle met également en cause l’implication présumée de Kigali aux côtés des rebelles du M23 dans l’est de la République démocratique du Congo (RDC). Des conséquences économiques inégales Une exclusion de l’AGOA entraînerait la perte des avantages douaniers accordés aux exportations des deux pays vers les États-Unis, qui seraient alors soumises aux tarifs habituels. Pour l’Afrique du Sud, les enjeux économiques sont particulièrement importants. En 2025, le pays a exporté pour environ 1,7 milliard de dollars de marchandises dans le cadre de ce programme, notamment des véhicules, des produits agricoles et du vin. La perspective de perdre ces avantages suscite des inquiétudes, particulièrement dans certains secteurs pourvoyeurs d’emplois, comme l’agrumiculture. Toutefois, le gouvernement sud-africain relativise les répercussions globales de cette éventuelle exclusion, estimant que les échanges concernés ne représentent qu'environ 10 % de son commerce avec les États-Unis. Pretoria envisage, par ailleurs, de renforcer ses relations commerciales avec d’autres partenaires, notamment la Chine, l’Inde et l’Union européenne. Pour le Rwanda, les conséquences économiques directes devraient être plus limitées. Ses exportations vers les États-Unis dans le cadre de l’AGOA, principalement constituées de café, de thé et de minerais, se sont élevées à environ 44 millions de dollars en 2025. L’enjeu apparaît donc davantage diplomatique et politique qu’économique. Une décision aux répercussions au-delà du commerce Si elle est effectivement mise en œuvre à la date annoncée, cette mesure marquera un nouveau tournant dans les relations commerciales entre Washington et les deux capitales africaines. Au-delà de la perte des préférences tarifaires, elle pourrait accentuer les tensions diplomatiques et pousser Pretoria comme Kigali à diversifier davantage leurs partenariats économiques. Le 1er janvier 2027 pourrait ainsi ouvrir une nouvelle séquence dans les relations entre les États-Unis et ces deux pays africains. Par Valentin SOMANDE L’article Les États-Unis menacent de bannir l’Afrique du Sud et le Rwanda de l’AGOA dès 2027 est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Two Techiman SHS teachers granted bail following arrest over student assault
items.description: The two teachers of Techiman Senior High School arrested over the viral assault of a 17-year-old Form 3 student have been granted bail by the Bono East Regional Police Command. The suspects, Jerry Jones Owusu Bekoe, a 37-year-old English teacher, and Ameyaw Adusa, a 44-year-old ICT teacher, were granted bail on Tuesday and are expected to reappear before the command on Wednesday. Sources at the school told Joy News that the two teachers met their bail conditions, and one of them was granted bail to enable him to sit for an examination scheduled for today. The Arrest and Investigation The two educators were arrested on November 1, after a viral video captured them assaulting the final-year student on campus. The footage sparked widespread outrage and prompted swift action from the police. In an exclusive interview with Joy News’ Anass Sabit, the Regional Commander, DCOP Shaibu A. Sadique-Osei, confirmed that investigations into the incident have commenced. “We have commenced investigations, and we are working to have further details into what preceded the assault by the teachers,” DCOP Sadique-Osei said. “They have given their account of the situation.” The Regional Commander indicated that the police are exploring all legal avenues and warned that the case could end up in court if a prima facie case is established. “If possible, the criminal aspect of the case will end in court if a prima facie case is established,” he stated. He also urged the public to remain calm and assured them that justice would be served. “The public should be calm and be assured that the matter will be addressed to its logical conclusion,” he added. Regarding the victim’s welfare, the Regional Commander confirmed that the student is receiving the necessary support. “The victim has been given the necessary psychological support, and the police are in touch with him,” he said. GES Investigates as School Engages Parents of Bullied Students The Ghana Education Service (GES) is also taking the matter seriously. The Municipal Director of Education, Isaac Amankwa, told Joy News that a committee has been set up at the school level to investigate the matter. “A team from the regional level is also working to have a full regional disciplinary committee to look into it,” Mr Amankwa said. He provided an update on the victim’s condition, stating that the student is responding to treatment at the Holy Family Hospital. “He complained of pains at the back of his head, but he is in a stable condition,” Mr Amankwa said. “GES will follow due administrative process to ensure that justice is served.” In a related development, the school is now engaging the parents of the two first-year students who were allegedly bullied by senior students—the incident that reportedly triggered the assault. Sources say the school authorities are working to address the situation and provide support to the affected first-year students, who earlier told Joy News off-camera that they have been left traumatised and wish to be taken out of the school. What Triggered the Assault? While the viral video captured the shocking moment of the assault, our checks have revealed a troubling chain of events that preceded it. Sources indicate that the two final-year students allegedly bullied two first-year students, subjecting them to severe beatings that made them roll on the floor seemingly for no apparent reason. It was this conduct that caught the attention of the two teachers, who, out of anger, went overboard in the now-viral video. The two first-year students who were beaten spoke to Joy News’ Anass Sabit, sharing their horrifying experience. They said what they went through has instilled fear in them, and they wish to be taken out of the school. What We Know So Far 1· The Incident: On October 23, 2026, at approximately 16:00 hours, the two teachers allegedly accosted the 17-year-old Form 3 student on campus and assaulted him. The teachers claimed the assault was in retaliation for the victim allegedly attacking two Form 1 students. 2· The Arrest: The two teachers were arrested on November 1, 2026, and were later granted bail after meeting their bail conditions. One of them was permitted to sit for an examination today. 3· The Reappearance: The two teachers are expected to reappear before the Bono East Regional Police Command on Wednesday. 4· The Investigations: The Bono East Regional Police Command has commenced investigations, and the GES has set up both school-level and regional-level committees to look into the matter. 5· The Victim: The 17-year-old student is responding to treatment at the Holy Family Hospital and is receiving psychological support. 6· The Bullied Students: The school is engaging the parents of the two first-year students who were allegedly bullied, as authorities work to address their situation and provide support. What Happens Next? The two teachers are scheduled to reappear before the police command on Wednesday as investigations continue. The police have indicated that the criminal aspect of the case will proceed to court if a prima facie case is established. Meanwhile, the GES has assured the public that due administrative processes will be followed to ensure justice is served. But questions remain: How did a case of alleged bullying escalate into an assault captured on camera? And what does this say about the culture of discipline in our schools? Both the police and GES say investigations will get to the bottom of it. Joy News will continue to follow this story and bring you updates as the investigations unfold.

items.title: AFCON 2027Q: Ibrahim Tanko ‘proud’ to be part of Black Stars interim technical team ahead of Somalia clash
items.description: Black Stars interim assistant coach Ibrahim Tanko has stated that he is proud and considers it an honour to step into the role to help the team bounce back from their difficult start to the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) qualifying campaign. Ghana suffered a disappointing start to the qualifiers in a 2-0 defeat to Côte d’Ivoire in Bouaké before losing 4-2 to Gambia at the Accra Sports Stadium. These back-to-back defeats eventually led to the Ghana Football Association (GFA) mutually parting ways with former head coach Carlos Queiroz. A five-member committee was set up by the GFA and the Ministry of Sports and Recreation to interview and recommend a new coach for the Black Stars. Ahead of the AFCON 2027 qualifiers, Kim Lars Björkegren was appointed to serve as the interim head coach, with Tanko, Godwin Attram serving as his assistants. Ghana prepares to face Somalia in a doubleheader in November, with the first game on November 12 and the second on November 16. In an interview with Joy Sports, Tanko, who also doubles up as head coach of Medeama, says that even though he is not happy about the current performance and results from the Black Stars, he still considers being called to help the national team as a privilege. “I am proud to be one of those who can help Ghana in this very tough situation.” “For me, national duty is something special. I have served Ghana in different capacities, and whenever the opportunity comes to contribute, I see it as a privilege. “The situation may be challenging, but we must be ready to give our best,” he stated. Ghana sits at the bottom of Group C and are hoping to get their qualifiers back on track, having missed out on the 2025 AFCON in Morocco. The interim technical team is expected to announce the squad this week as they gear up for their most decisive match.

items.title: Assemblée nationale : Comment «la question préalable» a entraîné le rejet des amendements de la LFR 2026
items.description: Le projet de loi de finances rectificative (LFR) a été rejeté à l’Assemblée nationale à la suite de l’adoption d’une question préalable soulevée par le député de Pastef, Amadou Ba. Cette procédure parlementaire a permis de mettre un terme à l’examen du texte sans que les députés ne se prononcent sur le fond. En invoquant cette disposition, le parlementaire a implicitement considéré qu’« il n’y a pas lieu à délibérer ». Une démarche qui revient à contester la nécessité même de poursuivre l’examen du projet de loi. Pour justifier son initiative, Amadou Ba a notamment mis en cause « la sincérité du budget ». La question préalable est encadrée par l’article 83 de la loi organique n° 2025-11 du 18 août 2025 portant Règlement intérieur de l’Assemblée nationale. Elle constitue un mécanisme de procédure permettant à un député de demander à la représentation nationale de décider qu’il n’y a pas lieu de poursuivre la délibération sur un texte soumis à son appréciation. Son adoption entraîne ainsi le rejet du texte concerné sans examen de ses dispositions sur le fond. C’est précisément ce qui s’est produit avec le projet de LFR, dont l’examen parlementaire a été interrompu à la suite du vote de la question préalable. Le scrutin a enregistré 109 voix favorables, 20 voix contre et 3 abstentions. Le recours à cet instrument parlementaire aura donc constitué le point décisif empêchant l’examen approfondi des mesures budgétaires proposées par le Gouvernement. O.BA

items.title: Finding Love In Accra Episode 4: Let me hear your voice
items.description: Read Also: Finding Love In Accra Episode 3: Typing… What did you delete last night? I sat up. Checked the message again. Then checked my ceiling, as though the answer might be up there. Nothing, I typed. Deleted. The evidence suggested otherwise. How do you know I deleted something? His reply came almost immediately. You were typing for a while. Then you disappeared. So he had been watching. I smiled. Then remembered I was under investigation. I couldn’t decide what to say. To me? That small question made me uncomfortable. There was a time I could call Kojo and begin a conversation halfway through a complaint. No greeting. No explanation. He would listen until he caught up. Now I was checking punctuation before speaking to him. It’s been a long time, I replied. He came online. Went offline. Came back. Please. We were both too grown for this hide-and-seek, and yet there I was, monitoring….. Then my phone rang. Kojo Campus. I let it ring twice so I wouldn’t appear desperate. On the third ring, I nearly dropped it. “Hello?” “Lovia.” “Yes?” “Breathe.” “I am breathing.” “Good. You seemed to be struggling with a text. I thought I’d make it easier.” I pulled my duvet over my knees. “You could have texted me too.” “I could have.” Silence. I had expected an explanation. Perhaps even a small apology. Instead, he waited. “I wasn’t very nice to you,” I said. “No. You weren’t.” Ei. No cushioning? No oh, don’t worry about it ? “I’m trying to apologise.” “I’m listening.” I picked at a loose thread on my pillowcase. “I should have answered when you asked me out. Even if I didn’t want to go. You deserved a reply.” “Thank you.” “I was immature.” “We both were young.” “You weren’t that immature.” He laughed softly. “You didn’t know everything about me.” For some reason, that bothered me. I had always thought I knew Kojo. His patience. His ridiculous handwriting. The way he rubbed his forehead when he was tired. But four years had happened without me. There were probably people who knew what he ate for breakfast now. “So,” he said, “what brought all this on?” I could have blamed the restaurant. The bracelet. Emefa. Instead, I told him. “I missed talking to you.” His voice softened. “Then you could have called.” “I know.” “Why didn’t you?” Because I liked believing you would always be happy to hear from me, and I was afraid to find out I was wrong. “I wasn’t sure you’d answer.” He let that sit between us. Then, “I answered tonight.” I smiled into my pillow. We talked. About my work. His move to a new apartment. A lecturer we both remembered who used to lock the lecture hall at exactly eight. At one point, I laughed so loudly I had to cover my mouth. “What?” he asked. “Nothing. I’d forgotten you were this funny.” “You used to laugh.” “I used to do a lot of things.” “Like call me your brother?” I closed my eyes. “Can we retire that?” “Already? I was getting used to the family.” “Kojo, please.” He laughed, and I wished he were sitting beside me. Then he yawned. I glanced at the time. We had been talking for fifty-three minutes. “You should sleep,” I said, hoping he would disagree. “Probably.” Disappointing man. “Goodnight, then.” “Goodnight, Lovia.” Neither of us ended the call. I listened to the quiet at his end. “Kojo?” “Hmm?” “Who was the woman at the restaurant?” A pause. Then I heard him laugh. “I was wondering when you’d ask.” “I’m just making conversation.” “At almost midnight?” “Goodnight.” “Lovia.” “What?” “Have dinner with me.” I stopped pulling at the thread. “Saturday?” “Yes.” “Just the two of us?” “Unless you’re bringing another relative.” I laughed. Then, before I could spend another four years finding the right response, I said yes. After we hung up, I changed his contact name. Deleted Campus . Looked at Kojo for a moment. Then added a heart. Removed it immediately. Let us get through dinner first. To be continued.

items.title: Five players who died after on-field incidents
items.description: Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel died on Tuesday as a result of injuries he suffered in a sickening collision with FC Andorra’s goalkeeper in a Spanish second division match. The 30-year-old is sadly not a unique case of a player dying either on the pitch or because of an injury sustained during the match. AFP Sport highlights five such fatalities: Marc-Vivien Foe, June 2003 Cameroon midfielder Foe collapsed after a heart attack during a Confederations Cup semi-final against Colombia in Lyon, France. The former Manchester City, West Ham and Lyon player was carried from the pitch as medical staff tried to revive him with mouth-to-mouth resuscitation and oxygen. After trying to restart his heart for 45 minutes without success he was declared dead, aged just 28. His death prompted improvements in both the testing of footballers for heart problems and the treatment they can receive during matches, including training club medical teams in CPR and using defibrillators. Antonio Puerta, August 2007 Spain international Puerta, 22, collapsed while playing for Sevilla in a La Liga match against Getafe and died three days later from multiple organ failure stemming from prolonged cardiac arrest. It was three months after he had helped Sevilla to win the UEFA Cup. Spanish legend Sergio Ramos has a tattoo tribute to Puerta and wore a T-shirt dedicated to him as Spain won the 2010 World Cup. “Antonio has always been with me. The next game, I went out on the field with his shirt and for a long time after that, I wore one that was dedicated to him,” said Ramos. Phil O’Donnell, December 2007 The Motherwell captain died of heart failure towards the end of his side’s 5-3 Scottish Premier League win over Dundee United in December 2007. The 35-year-old midfielder collapsed just as he was about to be substituted and was treated for around five minutes on the field before being taken to a waiting ambulance. O’Donnell played for Scotland, Celtic and Sheffield Wednesday during his career and his death caused widespread grief in Scottish football, causing a number of fixtures to be postponed. “He was a man among boys in every sense, in his attitude, his professionalism and integrity and sincerity,” his manager Mark McGhee said. Cristiano Junior, August 2009 The 25-year-old Brazilian, who was then the highest paid footballer in India, collided with the opposing goalkeeper when he scored a goal for his club Dempo 12 minutes from time in the 2004 Federation Cup final in Bangalore. Junior, who had moved to India to earn enough money to build a house for his mother back home, collapsed and was immediately attended to by his Nigerian strike partner Santi Martins. Martins stayed with him until an ambulance whisked him off to hospital but he was pronounced dead on arrival having suffered cardiac arrest. “The match continued. We played the remaining 12 minutes, received the trophy and were told of Cristiano’s death only when we reached the hospital. We broke down, unable to control ourselves,” his teammate and club captain Stanley Colaco told the Times of India in 2021. Juan Izquierdo, August 2024 The 27-year-old Uruguayan central defender suffered cardiac arrhythmia during his club Nacional’s Copa Libertadores last 16 match with Brazilian outfit Sao Paulo FC. Taken to hospital, he died five days later of “cardio respiratory arrest associated with his cardiac arrhythmia”. His second child had only been born 10 days prior to his death. His club described his death as an “irreplaceable loss”. Vanguard News The post Five players who died after on-field incidents appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Burkina: ce qu’il faut exiger lors des contrôles sur les normes environnementales des unités industrielles
items.description: Dans ce communiqué du ministère burkinabè de l'Agriculture, de l'Eau, des Ressources animales et halieutiques, publié ce mardi 3 novembre 2026, le Département ministériel, rassure tout mettre en œuvre pour éviter les contrôles non coordonnés pour le respect des normes environnementales dans les unités industrielles qui pénalisent les acteurs du domaine. En conséquence, le ministère invite les promoteurs et responsables d'unités industrielles à «exiger systématiquement la présentation de l'ordre de mission ou du mandat avant tout contrôle, ainsi qu'une quittance officielle pour tout paiement d'amende». COMMUNIQUE Le Ministre d'État, Ministre de l'Agriculture, de l'Eau, des Ressources animales et halieutiques porte à la connaissance des promoteurs et responsables d'unités industrielles que, dans le cadre de leurs missions de protection de l'environnement et des ressources en eau, la Police de l'eau, la Police de l'environnement et l'Agence nationale des évaluations environnementales (ANEVE) procèdent régulièrement à des opérations de contrôle et d'inspection au sein des établissements industriels. Toutefois, le Ministère a été saisi de préoccupations notamment relatives à la multiplicité des contrôles non coordonnés, à des pratiques présumées de rançonnement ainsi qu'à l'absence de délivrance de quittances à la suite de paiement de certaines amendes. Face à ces préoccupations et dans un souci de transparence, de redevabilité et de bonne conduite des opérations de contrôle, le Ministère rappelle et précise les dispositions suivantes : -la présentation obligatoire d'un ordre de mission: tout agent commis à un contrôle ou à une inspection doit, dès son arrivée, présenter un ordre de mission ou un mandat dûment signé par l'autorité compétente, précisant l'objet de la mission ainsi que l'identité des agents mandatés; -la délivrance systématique d'une quittance toute amende infligée à l'issue d'un contrôle doit faire l'objet d'un paiement donnant obligatoirement lieu à la délivrance d'une quittance officielle précisant le montant versé et le motif de l'infraction; -la coordination des interventions les structures compétentes sont instruites de privilégier des opérations conjointes et coordonnées afin de limiter les contrôles répétitifs et les interventions non concertées au sein des mêmes unités industrielles. En conséquence, le Ministère invite les promoteurs et responsables d'unités industrielles à exiger systématiquement la présentation de l'ordre de mission ou du mandat avant tout contrôle, ainsi qu'une quittance officielle pour tout paiement d'amende. Aucun paiement ne doit être effectué directement à un agent sans délivrance d'une pièce officielle justifiant le versement. Tout manquement à ces dispositions, toute tentative de rançonnement où tout comportement contraire à l'éthique professionnelle peut être signalé au numéro vert par appel ou whatsapp: 51 51 34 04. Le Ministère réaffirme sa disponibilité à accompagner les unités industrielles dans le respect de la réglementation environnementale en vigueur. Il réitère également sa ferme détermination à faire respecter les règles de contrôle et à prendre les mesures appropriées à l'encontre de tout auteur de pratiques irrégulières dûment établies. Le Ministère compte sur le sens de responsabilité et la collaboration de l'ensemble des acteurs pour des contrôles transparents, professionnels et respectueux de la réglementation. items.title: Soaring LPG prices force rickshaw drivers in Pakistan to cut meals
items.description: For 13 years, Rashid Ali has driven a three-wheeled motorised rickshaw around Lahore. His day starts at 6am and sometimes does not end until midnight, but he was long able to make around Rs1,700 ($6.50) a day, enough for his family’s bare essentials. Now, with liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) prices surging, he doesn’t even make half that. Ali, 33, is among thousands of drivers who run their vehicles on LPG, which is sold in cylinders and mainly used for cooking and heating. Rashid Ali waits for customers while offering rides in his liquefied petroleum gas (LPG)-powered auto-rickshaw along a road in Lahore, on October 30, 2026. — Reuters Majeed Ghauri, Chairman of the Awami Rickshaw Union, calls it “the fuel of the poor” and says about 70 per cent of its members’ 43,000 auto-rickshaws and nearly 8,000 Qingqi motorcycle-based three-wheelers, which carry several passengers on set routes, run on LPG. LPG prices have surged since October 17, when two Iranian border crossings closed , halting imports, traders say, in the latest energy shock since the US-Iran war began in February. One of the border crossings was opened a week later. With Ali now lucky to make around Rs800 ($3) a day, his family has cut back on meals, eating only twice a day. “Previously, when LPG was cheap, we could earn a decent income,” Ali said. “Now, it’s just not possible to get by on Rs700 or Rs800, is it?” A man fills a cylinder with liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) at his shop in Lahore on October 30, 2026. — Reuters Before the border closures, Pakistan imported about 7,000 metric tonnes of LPG a day from Iran, the Pakistan LPG Association said. Traders said the price of a 12-kilogramme cylinder jumped 56pc within days of the closure to Rs7,000, or about Rs583 rupees per kg in the open market. Walking away Ali pays Rs600 a day to rent his rickshaw, filling up with fuel four or five times a day, at Rs300 to Rs400 a time. As well as daily expenses, Ali also pays Rs11,000 a month for his home and has two young children to support. Adding to his problems, passengers, he said, do not want to pay higher fares. “For a trip that should cost Rs200 or Rs250, they might only offer Rs80, Rs100, or Rs150 rupees,” Ali said. Passenger Mohammad Ramzan said when a driver asked Rs500 rupees for a ride in the city, he offered half that. When the driver declined, he walked away, he said. Inflation hit 9.6pc in October and the central bank last week raised interest rates to 12pc, citing energy and wheat prices. Petrol hit a record Rs458 a litre on April 3 and remains about 40pc above its pre-war price. Back home at midday, Ali said his two boys still needed their lunch. He would go out again until late at night, he said, hoping to make enough to bring something for the children to eat at night. Rashid Ali is reflected in a side mirror as he drives his liquefied petroleum gas (LPG)-powered auto-rickshaw along a road in Lahore on October 30, 2026. — Reuters
